50f2c32bcf67.en: Here is a short piece of code on a machine that, like Part 7's pipeline, starts its instructions in program order. Each row is an instruction; time runs to the right, one column a cycle. <bookmark mark='a'/> The fifth instruction is a load, and its data is not in the cache: memory takes sixty cycles to answer. <bookmark mark='b'/> The add after it needs the loaded value, so it waits. That is unavoidable. <bookmark mark='c'/> But look at everything after the add. None of it uses the load. These instructions could have run at once, yet an in-order machine cannot start them until the add has started, so they all sit out the miss. <bookmark mark='d'/> Eighty-one cycles, for sixteen instructions.
50f2c32bcf67.zh: 这是一小段代码，运行在一台像第7部分的流水线那样按程序顺序开始执行指令的机器上。每一行是一条指令；时间向右走，一列是一个周期。<bookmark mark='a'/>第五条指令是一次取数，而它的数据不在缓存里：存储器要六十个周期才回答。<bookmark mark='b'/>它后面的加法需要读出的值，所以只能等。这无法避免。<bookmark mark='c'/>但看看加法后面的所有指令。它们没有一条用到这次取数。这些指令本可以马上执行，可一台按顺序执行的机器在加法开始之前不能开始它们，于是它们全都陪着这次缺失一起等。<bookmark mark='d'/>八十一个周期，只为了十六条指令。

e9e8674e2740.en: Now the same code on a machine that does not wait its turn. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every instruction starts as soon as its operands are ready. The load misses, as before, and the add waits for it, as before. But the ten instructions after the add have nothing to wait for, so they run in the next few cycles, underneath the miss. <bookmark mark='b'/> They finish long before the load, then wait, in the blue, for their turn to commit, because the machine still makes its results official in program order. When the load's data arrives, the add runs and everything commits in a rush. <bookmark mark='c'/> Seventy cycles instead of eighty-one, and every cycle of independent work was hidden behind the miss.
e9e8674e2740.zh: 现在把同样的代码放到一台不按次序排队的机器上。<bookmark mark='a'/>每条指令一旦操作数就绪就开始执行。取数照样缺失，加法照样等它。但加法后面的十条指令没有什么要等的，所以它们在接下来几个周期里就执行完了，就在缺失的底下。<bookmark mark='b'/>它们远早于取数完成，然后在蓝色里等着轮到自己提交，因为机器仍然按程序顺序让结果生效。取数的数据一到，加法执行，所有指令一拥而上地提交。<bookmark mark='c'/>七十个周期而不是八十一个，而且每个周期的独立工作都藏在了缺失的背后。

89f8b526cec9.en: Scale that up to the Job. Its first chapter runs eight hundred twenty-seven thousand instructions. <bookmark mark='a'/> Part 7's pipeline took about a million cycles: an IPC, instructions per cycle, of zero point eight three. <bookmark mark='b'/> This part's core, forced to start its instructions one at a time and in program order, does a little worse: its front end is deeper than the pipeline's, so a wrong guess about a branch costs it more. <bookmark mark='c'/> The same core, allowed to look ahead and start up to four ready instructions a cycle, takes four hundred thirty-eight thousand cycles. An IPC of almost one point nine. <bookmark mark='d'/> Nothing about the instructions changed, nor the adders, nor the memory. Only the order in which work is started.
89f8b526cec9.zh: 把它放大到任务上。任务的第一章执行八十二万七千条指令。<bookmark mark='a'/>第7部分的流水线用了大约一百万个周期：每周期指令数，也就是 IPC，为零点八三。<bookmark mark='b'/>这一部分的处理器核，如果强迫它一条一条、按程序顺序开始执行指令，会稍差一点：它的前端比流水线更深，所以一次分支猜错代价更大。<bookmark mark='c'/>同一个核，允许它向前看、每个周期开始最多四条就绪的指令，只用四十三万八千个周期。IPC 接近一点九。<bookmark mark='d'/>指令没有变，存储器也没有变。变的只是机器一次能开始多少工作，以及按什么顺序。

4af9b2f9bb3a.en: The machine that did this can hold a hundred twenty-eight instructions in flight at once, in a structure called the reorder buffer. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is how many it actually holds, cycle by cycle, over six hundred cycles of the Job. <bookmark mark='b'/> It climbs, and then it crashes to zero; climbs and crashes. On average, about eleven instructions are in flight, and the buffer is never once full. <bookmark mark='c'/> Real cores keep far more: Intel's Golden Cove core of 2021 has five hundred twelve entries. Why build such a huge window, and what keeps knocking ours down to zero? Both answers are in this part, and the second one is the most important fact about modern processors.
4af9b2f9bb3a.zh: 做到这一点的机器可以同时容纳一百二十八条在途的指令，放在一个叫重排序缓冲区的结构里。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是它在任务的六百个周期里实际容纳的数量，一个周期一个周期地画出来。<bookmark mark='b'/>它爬上去，然后跌到零；再爬上去，再跌下来。平均只有大约十一条指令在途，缓冲区一次也没有满过。<bookmark mark='c'/>真实的处理器核容纳得多得多：英特尔 2021 年的 Golden Cove 核有五百一十二项。为什么要造这么大的窗口？又是什么不停地把我们的窗口打回零？两个答案都在这一部分里，而第二个是关于现代处理器最重要的事实。

72fe3772899d.en: Here is where this part goes. <bookmark mark='a'/> First, a limit: given a program, how fast could any machine run it, if only the true dependences between its instructions mattered? <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the machines that approach that limit: the scoreboard of 1964, Tomasulo's algorithm of 1967, register renaming, and the reorder buffer, built here and checked against the emulator. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then speculation, the guess that lets a core run hundreds of instructions ahead of what it knows. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then the price of guessing: in 2018 it was shown that the guesses leave traces a program can read, and we will read a secret on our own machine. <bookmark mark='e'/> And the Job, run on the new core, for the next row of the ledger.
72fe3772899d.zh: 这一部分要去的地方是这样的。<bookmark mark='a'/>首先是一个极限：给定一个程序，如果只有指令之间的真依赖起作用，任何机器最快能跑多快？<bookmark mark='b'/>然后是逼近这个极限的机器：1964 年的记分牌，1967 年的托马苏洛算法，寄存器重命名，以及重排序缓冲区，在这里造出来，并与仿真器核对。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后是推测执行，正是这种猜测让一个核能在它确知的东西前面跑出几百条指令。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后是猜测的代价：2018 年人们证明，这些猜测会留下程序能读出的痕迹，我们将在自己的机器上读出一个秘密。<bookmark mark='e'/>最后，任务在新核上运行，给出账本的下一行。

4b2b46958f4b.en: This is Part 8 of Computer Science, Built, the second part of Act Two, Making It Fast. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: the dataflow graph of a program, its critical path, and the limit it sets. True and false dependences, and register renaming, which removes the false ones. The scoreboard of the CDC 6600 and Tomasulo's algorithm, cycle by cycle. The reorder buffer, which lets a machine execute out of order yet keep its exceptions precise. Superscalar issue and the wall it hits, speculation, and the ordering of loads and stores. Then Spectre, the compiler's alternative called VLIW, the old argument between RISC and CISC, multithreading, and the Job.
4b2b46958f4b.zh: 这是《计算机科学，从零搭建》的第8部分，第二幕“让它变快”的第二部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分讲：程序的数据流图、它的关键路径，以及它设下的极限。真依赖与假依赖，以及消除假依赖的寄存器重命名。CDC 6600 的记分牌和托马苏洛算法，一个周期一个周期地看。重排序缓冲区，它让机器乱序执行却保持异常精确。超标量发射和它撞上的墙、推测执行，以及取数与存数的顺序。然后是幽灵漏洞、编译器的另一条路超长指令字、精简与复杂指令集之间的老争论、多线程，以及任务。

e024745e0d91.en: In Part 7 we found where the Job spends its time: in one small loop, the scan of the word table. For every word it reads, the Job walks the table entry by entry, skipping each entry whose length differs from the word's. <bookmark mark='a'/> Six instructions a trip: test whether the table is finished, load this entry's length, compare it, step to the next entry, count, and jump back. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the pipeline a trip took seven cycles. <bookmark mark='c'/> So here is this chapter's question. Forget pipelines and forget hardware. If a machine could start any instruction the moment its inputs exist, how fast could this loop go?
e024745e0d91.zh: 在第7部分我们找到了任务把时间花在哪里：一个小循环，对单词表的扫描。每读一个词，任务就逐项走过整张表，跳过长度和这个词不同的每一项。<bookmark mark='a'/>每趟六条指令：检查表是否走完，取出这一项的长度，比较它，走到下一项，计数，跳回去。<bookmark mark='b'/>在流水线上一趟要七个周期。<bookmark mark='c'/>于是这一章的问题是：忘掉流水线，也忘掉硬件。如果一台机器能在任何一条指令的输入出现的那一刻就开始它，这个循环最快能跑多快？

c26c4c457d25.en: Draw each instruction as a node, and an arrow from the instruction that produces a value to each one that uses it. This is the program's dataflow graph: the only order that really matters. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are four trips round the loop, each instruction placed in the earliest cycle it could start. Loads take two cycles, everything else one. The four jumps depend on nothing at all, so they are left out of the picture. <bookmark mark='b'/> The load of an entry's length needs only the entry's address, and the branch needs only the load. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the address of the next entry needs only the address of this one. That is the chain that runs through all four trips: one add per trip, each waiting for the last. <bookmark mark='d'/> The longest chain of dependences through the graph is called the critical path. Here it is six cycles long, so no machine, however wide, can do these four trips in fewer than six cycles. The pipeline took twenty-eight.
c26c4c457d25.zh: 把每条指令画成一个节点，从产生一个值的指令向每条用到它的指令画一个箭头。这就是程序的数据流图：唯一真正重要的顺序。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里是循环的四趟，每条指令都放在它最早可以开始的周期里。取数要两个周期，其余都是一个。四条跳转指令什么也不依赖，所以没有画进图里。<bookmark mark='b'/>取出一项长度的取数只需要这一项的地址，而分支只需要取数。<bookmark mark='c'/>下一项的地址只需要这一项的地址。这就是贯穿四趟的那条链：每趟一次加法，每次都等上一次。<bookmark mark='d'/>图中最长的依赖链叫关键路径。这里它长六个周期，所以没有机器，不管多宽，能用少于六个周期做完这四趟。流水线用了二十八个。

707879eaa3d0.en: The critical path assumes a machine that can start as many instructions in a cycle as it likes. Real machines have a width: so many instructions a cycle, and no more. Picture the machine as a grid, one row for each slot, one column for each cycle. <bookmark mark='a'/> One wide, the twenty-four instructions, jumps included, need twenty-four cycles. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two wide: twelve. <bookmark mark='c'/> Four wide: seven, one more than the critical path. <bookmark mark='d'/> Eight wide: six, and now most slots are empty; the width no longer matters, only the chain does. <bookmark mark='e'/> Two things bound the time, then: the work divided by the width, and the length of the longest chain.
707879eaa3d0.zh: 关键路径假设机器一个周期想开始多少条指令都行。真实的机器有宽度：每个周期最多开始那么多条。把机器想象成一张网格，每个发射槽一行，每个周期一列。<bookmark mark='a'/>一条宽时，二十四条指令，连同跳转在内，需要二十四个周期。<bookmark mark='b'/>两条宽：十二个。<bookmark mark='c'/>四条宽：七个，比关键路径多一个。<bookmark mark='d'/>八条宽：六个，而且现在大多数槽都空着；宽度不再重要，只有那条链重要。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以时间受两样东西约束：工作量除以宽度，以及最长链的长度。

adace92e5532.en: Those two bounds have names. The number of instructions is the work, N. The critical path is the span, L. With a width W, <bookmark mark='a'/> no schedule can take fewer cycles than the work divided by the width, and none can beat the span. <bookmark mark='b'/> And there is a matching upper bound, proved by Ronald Graham in 1966 for scheduling jobs on machines: any greedy schedule, one that never leaves a slot idle while some instruction is ready, finishes within N over W plus L. The greedy schedule is never worse than twice the best. <bookmark mark='c'/> Our four trips obey both, at every width. <bookmark mark='d'/> And in a loop the span becomes a rate. The longest chain gains one add per trip, so in the steady state the loop could run one trip per cycle, six instructions a cycle. The pipeline manages zero point eight six. Between those numbers lies everything this part is about.
adace92e5532.zh: 这两个界都有名字。指令的条数是工作量，N。关键路径是跨度，L。宽度为 W 时，<bookmark mark='a'/>没有调度能比工作量除以宽度更快，也没有调度能胜过跨度。<bookmark mark='b'/>还有一个对应的上界，由罗纳德·格雷厄姆在 1966 年为机器上的作业调度证明：任何贪心调度，也就是只要有就绪的指令就从不让槽空着的调度，都在 N 除以 W 加 L 之内完成。贪心调度从来不会比最好的差两倍以上。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们的四趟在每个宽度上都满足这两个界。<bookmark mark='d'/>在循环里，跨度变成了速率。最长的链每趟多一次加法，所以在稳定状态下循环可以每周期跑一趟，每周期六条指令。流水线只做到零点八六。这一部分要讲的一切，都在这两个数字之间。

a45babf4c08c.en: Chapter two. False dependences, and renaming.
a45babf4c08c.zh: 第二章。假依赖与重命名。

2ca093a2b5a1.en: Not every ordering between two instructions is real. Take these five. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first loads a0 and the second adds it to itself. The add needs the value the load produced: a read after a write, a true dependence. Data flows along it, and no machine can run the add first. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now the third instruction loads a new value into a0. It must not overwrite a0 before the add has read the old one: a write after a read. <bookmark mark='c'/> And it must not land before the first load either, or the first load's later write would clobber it: a write after a write. <bookmark mark='d'/> But look at what these last two are about. No value passes from one instruction to the other. They exist only because two different values happen to share one register's name. The second half of this code, which works on a completely new value, is chained to the first half by nothing but a name.
2ca093a2b5a1.zh: 两条指令之间的顺序并不都是真的。看这五条。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一条把值取进 a0，第二条把它和自己相加。加法需要取数产生的那个值：写后读，一个真依赖。数据沿着它流动，没有机器能先执行加法。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在第三条指令把一个新值取进 a0。在加法读走旧值之前，它不能覆盖 a0：读后写。<bookmark mark='c'/>它也不能落在第一条取数之前，否则第一条取数后来的写会把它冲掉：写后写。<bookmark mark='d'/>但看看后两种讲的是什么。没有任何值从一条指令传到另一条。它们之所以存在，只是因为两个不同的值碰巧共用了一个寄存器的名字。这段代码的后一半处理的是一个全新的值，把它和前一半拴在一起的，只有一个名字。

febf4620a4a5.en: How common are the false ones? Count them over the eight hundred twenty-seven thousand instructions of the Job's first chapter. <bookmark mark='a'/> Nine hundred eighty thousand true dependences, values flowing from one instruction to another. <bookmark mark='b'/> And more than nine hundred thousand false ones, half of them writes after reads and half writes after writes. <bookmark mark='c'/> They are everywhere for a simple reason: Pebble has only fifteen registers to name values with, so every register holds a long succession of different values, and each reuse ties the new value to the old.
febf4620a4a5.zh: 假依赖有多常见？在任务第一章的八十二万七千条指令上数一数。<bookmark mark='a'/>九十八万个真依赖，也就是从一条指令流向另一条的值。<bookmark mark='b'/>还有九十多万个假依赖，一半是读后写，一半是写后写。<bookmark mark='c'/>它们无处不在，原因很简单：Pebble 只有十五个寄存器可以给值命名，所以每个寄存器都先后装着一长串不同的值，每次重用都把新值和旧值拴在一起。

8714d45e8bf4.en: The cure is to stop sharing names. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give the machine many more registers than the instruction set names: physical registers, p twenty, p twenty-one, and so on. Keep a small table, the register alias table, that says which physical register currently holds each architectural one. <bookmark mark='b'/> As each instruction arrives, in program order, its sources are looked up in the table, and its destination gets a fresh physical register, which the table then records. The load writes p twenty; the add reads p twenty and writes p twenty-one. <bookmark mark='c'/> The second load of a0 gets p twenty-two, a different register, so it can run whenever it likes: there is no old value for it to destroy. <bookmark mark='d'/> After renaming, no physical register is written twice. The anti and output dependences are gone, and the two halves of the code, two independent chains, can run side by side. Only the arrows that carry data are left.
8714d45e8bf4.zh: 解药是不再共用名字。<bookmark mark='a'/>给机器比指令集所命名的多得多的寄存器：物理寄存器，p 二十、p 二十一，等等。再保留一张小表，寄存器别名表，记录每个体系结构寄存器现在由哪个物理寄存器保存。<bookmark mark='b'/>每条指令按程序顺序到来时，在表里查出它的源操作数，再给它的目的寄存器分配一个新的物理寄存器，并记进表里。取数写 p 二十；加法读 p 二十，写 p 二十一。<bookmark mark='c'/>第二次取数到 a0 得到 p 二十二，一个不同的寄存器，所以它想什么时候执行都行：没有旧值会被它毁掉。<bookmark mark='d'/>重命名之后，没有哪个物理寄存器被写两次。反依赖和输出依赖都消失了，代码的两半，两条独立的链，可以并排执行。只剩下传送数据的箭头。

06f69f54d296.en: How much does that matter? Imagine an oracle: a machine with unlimited width that knows the whole run in advance, so it can start every instruction the moment its inputs exist. <bookmark mark='a'/> With every value in its own register, it runs the Job's first chapter at two thousand four hundred instructions per cycle. Different words' searches through the table do not depend on each other, so the oracle runs hundreds of them at once. <bookmark mark='b'/> Hold the same oracle to the false dependences, so that a register may not be rewritten until its old value is dead, and it manages three point seven. <bookmark mark='c'/> Renaming is worth a factor of more than six hundred, in the limit. Real machines are nowhere near either number, and chapter six will say why. But every fast general-purpose core built since the mid-1990s renames its registers.
06f69f54d296.zh: 这有多重要？想象一个先知：一台宽度无限、事先知道整个运行过程的机器，所以它可以在每条指令的输入出现的那一刻就开始它。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个值都有自己的寄存器时，它以每周期两千四百条指令的速度跑完任务第一章。不同单词在表里的查找互不依赖，所以先知同时跑几百个。<bookmark mark='b'/>让同一个先知遵守假依赖，也就是一个寄存器要等它的旧值不再有用才能改写，它只做到三点七。<bookmark mark='c'/>在极限情形下，重命名值六百多倍。真实的机器离这两个数都很远，第六章会说明原因。但二十世纪九十年代中期以来造出的每一个快速通用处理器核，都对寄存器做重命名。

3fb8bb0062fb.en: The first machine to let instructions overtake each other was the Control Data 6600, delivered in 1964, designed by Seymour Cray with James Thornton. <bookmark mark='a'/> It had ten functional units: adders, two multipliers, a divider, units for shifts, logic, branches and address arithmetic, all able to work at once. <bookmark mark='b'/> The trouble with ten units is keeping them busy without getting the answers wrong. Thornton's solution was a central piece of bookkeeping called the scoreboard, which tracks every instruction in flight, every unit, and every register a unit is about to write. <bookmark mark='c'/> With a hundred-nanosecond clock it did up to three million operations a second, and it was the fastest computer in the world for five years. IBM's president, Thomas Watson Junior, wrote a famous memo asking how a laboratory of thirty-four people, including the janitor, had beaten IBM. Cray is said to have replied that Mr. Watson had answered his own question.
3fb8bb0062fb.zh: 第一台让指令互相超车的机器，是 1964 年交付的控制数据公司 6600，由西摩·克雷和詹姆斯·桑顿设计。<bookmark mark='a'/>它有十个功能部件：加法器、两个乘法器、一个除法器，还有做移位、逻辑、分支和地址运算的部件，全都可以同时工作。<bookmark mark='b'/>十个部件的麻烦在于，既要让它们都忙起来，又不能算错。桑顿的办法是一份集中的账本，叫记分牌，它记录每条在途的指令、每个部件，以及每个部件将要写的每个寄存器。<bookmark mark='c'/>它的时钟是一百纳秒，每秒最多做三百万次运算，在五年里一直是世界上最快的计算机。IBM 总裁小托马斯·沃森写过一份著名的备忘录，问一个连看门人在内只有三十四人的实验室，怎么会打败 IBM。据说克雷回答，沃森先生已经回答了他自己的问题。

729bae0cc384.en: Each instruction passes through four steps, and the scoreboard checks one kind of hazard at each. <bookmark mark='a'/> Issue happens in program order. An instruction issues when its kind of unit is free, and when no instruction already in flight is going to write the same register; that is the write after write hazard, and the 6600 simply refuses to have two writers of one name. <bookmark mark='b'/> Next, read operands. The instruction waits at its unit until every register it reads has been written by whoever was producing it: the true dependence. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then it executes, taking as many cycles as its unit needs. <bookmark mark='d'/> Last, write result. Before overwriting its destination, it waits until every earlier instruction that still needs the old value has read it: the write after read hazard. <bookmark mark='e'/> Notice that values travel only through the registers. Every hazard is a wait; nothing is renamed.
729bae0cc384.zh: 每条指令经过四步，记分牌在每一步检查一种冒险。<bookmark mark='a'/>发射按程序顺序进行。当一条指令所需种类的部件空闲，而且没有在途的指令将要写同一个寄存器时，它才发射；这就是写后写冒险，6600 干脆不允许同一个名字同时有两个写者。<bookmark mark='b'/>接着是读操作数。指令在它的部件前等着，直到它读的每个寄存器都已被产生它的指令写好：真依赖。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后它执行，部件需要几个周期就花几个周期。<bookmark mark='d'/>最后是写结果。在覆盖目的寄存器之前，它要等每条还需要旧值的更早的指令都读完：读后写冒险。<bookmark mark='e'/>注意，值只通过寄存器传递。每种冒险都是一次等待；没有任何东西被重命名。

898946206c1a.en: Here is the standard example from Hennessy and Patterson's textbook, written in Pebble's registers, with their latencies: a load takes one cycle, an add two, a multiply ten, a divide forty. <bookmark mark='a'/> Watch the scoreboard fill in the cycle at which each instruction completes each step. The first load issues in cycle one, reads in two, executes in three, writes in four. <bookmark mark='b'/> The second load cannot even issue until cycle five: there is only one integer unit, and the first load holds it until its result is written. <bookmark mark='c'/> The multiply and the subtract both wait for the second load, then read their operands together in cycle nine. The divide needs the multiply's result, so it waits at its unit until cycle twenty-one. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the last add. It issues in thirteen, when the adder is free, and its result is ready by sixteen. But it writes a1, and the divide, an earlier instruction, has not yet read the old a1. So the add sits on its finished result until cycle twenty-two. <bookmark mark='e'/> The whole thing takes sixty-two cycles.
898946206c1a.zh: 这是轩尼诗和帕特森教科书里的标准例子，用 Pebble 的寄存器写出，采用他们的延迟：取数一个周期，加法两个，乘法十个，除法四十个。<bookmark mark='a'/>看记分牌填出每条指令完成每一步的周期。第一条取数在第一周期发射，第二周期读操作数，第三周期执行，第四周期写回。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二条取数直到第五周期才能发射：只有一个整数部件，第一条取数一直占着它，直到结果写完。<bookmark mark='c'/>乘法和减法都在等第二条取数，然后在第九周期一起读操作数。除法需要乘法的结果，所以在它的部件前一直等到第二十一周期。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有最后的加法。它在第十三周期加法器空出时发射，结果在第十六周期就算好了。但它要写 a1，而更早的除法还没有读旧的 a1。于是加法守着算好的结果，一直等到第二十二周期。<bookmark mark='e'/>整段一共六十二个周期。

d96c244c8b7e.en: The scoreboard was a brilliant first step, and it has three limits. <bookmark mark='a'/> It handles false dependences by waiting. Two writers of one register cannot both be in flight, and a finished result can be held up, as our add was, by an earlier reader of the old value. <bookmark mark='b'/> Values pass only through the register file, so a result must be written before its user can read it. <bookmark mark='c'/> And issue is in order, so when one instruction cannot issue, nothing behind it can. <bookmark mark='d'/> Three years later, a team at IBM removed all three limits at once.
d96c244c8b7e.zh: 记分牌是出色的第一步，但它有三个局限。<bookmark mark='a'/>它靠等待来处理假依赖。同一个寄存器的两个写者不能同时在途，一个算好的结果也可能被某个读旧值的更早的指令拖住，就像我们的加法那样。<bookmark mark='b'/>值只能经过寄存器堆传递，所以结果必须先写进去，使用者才能读。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且发射是按顺序的，一条指令发射不了，它后面的都发射不了。<bookmark mark='d'/>三年之后，IBM 的一个团队一举去掉了这三个局限。

bb5446a0fd84.en: In 1967 IBM shipped the System/360 Model 91, a machine built for scientific computing. <bookmark mark='a'/> Its floating-point unit had a problem far worse than Pebble's: only four floating-point registers in the instruction set, so the same few names were reused constantly, and a scoreboard would have stalled on false dependences all the time. <bookmark mark='b'/> Robert Tomasulo's answer was to stop naming values by registers at all. A value in flight is named by the reservation station, a small waiting area in front of a functional unit, of the instruction that will produce it. <bookmark mark='c'/> An instruction waiting in a station holds, for each operand, either the value itself or the tag of the station that will produce it. <bookmark mark='d'/> And when a unit finishes, it broadcasts the result and its tag on a common data bus. Every station and the register file listen, and whoever is waiting for that tag takes the value. This is register renaming, done in 1967 with a handful of tags.
bb5446a0fd84.zh: 1967 年，IBM 交付了 System/360 Model 91，一台为科学计算而造的机器。<bookmark mark='a'/>它的浮点部件有一个比 Pebble 糟糕得多的问题：指令集里只有四个浮点寄存器，同样几个名字被不断重用，记分牌会一直卡在假依赖上。<bookmark mark='b'/>罗伯特·托马苏洛的答案是干脆不再用寄存器给值命名。一个在途的值，用将要产生它的那条指令所在的保留站来命名；保留站是功能部件前面一个小小的等候区。<bookmark mark='c'/>在保留站里等待的指令，对每个操作数要么持有值本身，要么持有将要产生它的保留站的标签。<bookmark mark='d'/>部件完成时，把结果和它的标签广播到一条公共数据总线上。每个保留站和寄存器堆都在听，谁在等这个标签，谁就把值取走。这就是寄存器重命名，1967 年就用一把标签做到了。

0f643d3960c0.en: Here is the machine. On the left, the instructions waiting to issue, in order. In the middle, the reservation stations: three for loads, three in front of the adder, two in front of the multiplier and divider. Below them the units, and under everything the common data bus, which runs back to every station and to the registers. <bookmark mark='a'/> Cycle one: the first load issues into Load1, and the register a1 now records that its next value will come from Load1. Cycle two: the second load issues, and a2 points at Load2. <bookmark mark='b'/> Cycle three: the multiply issues. Its operand a2 is not ready, so the station takes the tag Load2 instead. And the first load broadcasts: tag Load1 and its value go out on the bus, and a1 takes it. <bookmark mark='c'/> Cycle four: Load2 broadcasts, and the multiply, which was waiting for that tag, captures the value. The subtract issues with both its values in hand. <bookmark mark='d'/> Cycle five: the divide issues, waiting on tag Mult1, and holding the current value of a1. Cycle six: the last add issues. It will write a1, so a1 now points at Add2, but the divide does not care: it has already copied the old a1. That is the write after read hazard, gone. <bookmark mark='e'/> The subtract broadcasts in cycle seven, the add starts in the next cycle, and it broadcasts in cycle ten, while the multiply is still working. <bookmark mark='f'/> The multiply finishes in fifteen and its broadcast wakes the divide, which takes forty cycles and broadcasts in fifty-six.
0f643d3960c0.zh: 这就是这台机器。左边是等待发射的指令，按顺序排着。中间是保留站：三个给取数，三个在加法器前，两个在乘除法器前。下面是功能部件，最底下是公共数据总线，它通回每个保留站和寄存器。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一周期：第一条取数发射进 Load1，寄存器 a1 记下它的下一个值将来自 Load1。第二周期：第二条取数发射，a2 指向 Load2。<bookmark mark='b'/>第三周期：乘法发射。它的操作数 a2 还没好，所以保留站记下标签 Load2。同时第一条取数广播：标签 Load1 和它的值出现在总线上，a1 把它取走。<bookmark mark='c'/>第四周期：Load2 广播，一直在等这个标签的乘法捕获了这个值。减法发射，两个值都已在手。<bookmark mark='d'/>第五周期：除法发射，等着标签 Mult1，并持有 a1 的当前值。第六周期：最后的加法发射。它会写 a1，所以 a1 现在指向 Add2，但除法不在乎：它已经抄下了旧的 a1。这就是读后写冒险，消失了。<bookmark mark='e'/>减法在第七周期广播，加法在下一个周期开始，并在第十周期广播，那时乘法还在算。<bookmark mark='f'/>乘法在第十五周期完成，它的广播唤醒了除法，除法花四十个周期，在第五十六周期广播。

e0dfd84bbf48.en: Side by side. <bookmark mark='a'/> Most results arrive a little earlier, because the bus hands a value straight to the stations waiting for it, with no write and read through the register file. <bookmark mark='b'/> And the last add finishes twelve cycles sooner: under Tomasulo nobody waits for an earlier reader, because every reader has already copied what it needs. <bookmark mark='c'/> Fifty-six cycles instead of sixty-two. The divide's forty cycles dominate both, as they should: that is this example's critical path.
e0dfd84bbf48.zh: 并排对比。<bookmark mark='a'/>大多数结果都早到一点，因为总线把值直接交给等着它的保留站，不用经过寄存器堆写一次再读一次。<bookmark mark='b'/>最后的加法早了十二个周期完成：在托马苏洛算法下，没有谁要等更早的读者，因为每个读者都已经抄下了它需要的东西。<bookmark mark='c'/>五十六个周期而不是六十二个。除法的四十个周期在两者中都占主导，这理所当然：那是这个例子的关键路径。

c33a1c572f54.en: There is a catch, and it is serious. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is when each instruction's result reached the registers: the add in cycle ten, the divide in fifty-six. Program order says the divide comes first. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now suppose the divide divides by zero. The machine discovers this in cycle fifty-five, and wants to stop with every earlier instruction done and every later one untouched, so the operating system can report the error, or fix it and resume. <bookmark mark='c'/> But the add, a later instruction, overwrote a1 forty-five cycles ago. There is no moment between the divide and the add at which the registers were ever in a consistent state. The exception is imprecise. The Model 91 lived with this; its manuals warned programmers that a floating-point error could be reported some instructions late. For general-purpose machines with virtual memory, where any load may fault and must be restarted, it is not acceptable. The fix took eighteen years.
c33a1c572f54.zh: 这里有个问题，而且很严重。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是每条指令的结果到达寄存器的时间：加法在第十周期，除法在第五十六周期。程序顺序说除法在前。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在假设除法除以零。机器在第五十五周期发现这一点，它想停在这样一个状态：所有更早的指令都已完成，所有更晚的指令都没动过，这样操作系统才能报告错误，或者修好它再继续。<bookmark mark='c'/>但加法，一条更晚的指令，四十五个周期前就已经覆盖了 a1。在除法和加法之间，寄存器从来没有处于一个一致的状态。这个异常是不精确的。Model 91 就这样将就着用；它的手册警告程序员，浮点错误可能会晚几条指令才报告。对于有虚拟存储器、任何一次取数都可能出错并且必须重新开始的通用机器来说，这是不能接受的。修好它花了十八年。

2529457e41ac.en: In 1985 James Smith and Andrew Pleszkun proposed the fix, and every out-of-order core since has used it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Bring instructions in, in program order. Let them execute in whatever order their operands allow. But then put them back in order before anything they did becomes official. <bookmark mark='b'/> The last step is called commit, or retirement. Until an instruction commits, its result is held aside, visible to the instructions that need it but not yet written into the architectural registers or memory. <bookmark mark='c'/> Commit happens strictly oldest first. So at any moment, the official state of the machine is exactly what it would be if the instructions had run one at a time, in order, up to the oldest one still in flight.
2529457e41ac.zh: 1985 年，詹姆斯·史密斯和安德鲁·普莱什昆提出了修复办法，此后的每一个乱序核都在用它。<bookmark mark='a'/>按程序顺序把指令带进来。让它们按操作数允许的任何顺序执行。但在它们做的任何事情生效之前，把它们重新排回顺序。<bookmark mark='b'/>最后一步叫提交，或者叫退休。一条指令提交之前，它的结果被放在一边，需要它的指令看得见，但还没有写进体系结构寄存器或存储器。<bookmark mark='c'/>提交严格从最老的开始。所以任何时刻，机器的正式状态都恰好等于这些指令一次一条、按顺序执行到仍在途的最老那条为止时的样子。

919597d449ae.en: Here is the structure that does this, the reorder buffer, drawn as what it is: a ring of slots. <bookmark mark='a'/> These are about thirty cycles of the core running the Job's scan loop. Each cycle, up to four instructions are renamed and take slots at the tail, in program order. They wait, in orange, for their operands; execute, in green; and when finished, turn blue and wait. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each cycle, up to four finished instructions leave from the head, but only from the head: a finished instruction behind an unfinished one must wait for it. <bookmark mark='c'/> Watch the grey ones. The machine guessed wrong about a branch and fetched down a wrong path. When the branch executes and the mistake is found, everything younger than it is simply dropped from the ring: none of it had committed, so none of it ever happened. The tail jumps back to just after the branch, and fetching resumes on the right path.
919597d449ae.zh: 这就是做这件事的结构，重排序缓冲区，画成它本来的样子：一个由槽组成的环。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是处理器核运行任务扫描循环时大约三十个周期的情形。每个周期，最多四条指令被重命名，按程序顺序占据尾部的槽。它们在橙色里等操作数；在绿色里执行；完成后变成蓝色等着。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个周期，最多四条完成的指令从头部离开，但只能从头部：一条完成的指令如果排在一条没完成的后面，就必须等它。<bookmark mark='c'/>注意那些灰色的。机器对一个分支猜错了，沿着错误的路径取了指令。分支执行、发现错误时，比它年轻的一切都直接从环里丢掉：它们都还没提交，所以都不曾发生。尾指针跳回到分支后面，取指从正确的路径重新开始。

5b372bb30a83.en: Now the problem that defeated the Model 91. Here a divide by zero sits in the middle of some code, followed by instructions that use other values. <bookmark mark='a'/> The divide is slow: sixteen cycles. <bookmark mark='b'/> Meanwhile the four instructions after it execute and finish, including a store. They are done, in blue, but they are behind the divide in the reorder buffer, so they wait. <bookmark mark='c'/> When the divide reaches the head, the machine finds that it faulted. And at that moment everything older has committed and nothing younger has: so it discards the younger instructions, and reports the exception with the state exactly as it was just before the divide. <bookmark mark='d'/> The store before the divide reached memory. The store after it, which had already computed its address and data, never did. The exception is precise, though execution was not in order.
5b372bb30a83.zh: 现在来看难倒 Model 91 的那个问题。这里一条除以零的除法夹在一段代码中间，后面跟着一些用其他值的指令。<bookmark mark='a'/>除法很慢：十六个周期。<bookmark mark='b'/>与此同时，它后面的四条指令执行完了，其中包括一次存数。它们已经完成，显示为蓝色，但在重排序缓冲区里排在除法后面，所以只能等。<bookmark mark='c'/>除法到达头部时，机器发现它出错了。而此刻，所有更老的指令都已提交，所有更年轻的都没有：于是机器丢弃年轻的指令，报告这个异常，状态恰好是除法之前的样子。<bookmark mark='d'/>除法之前的存数到达了存储器。除法之后的存数，虽然已经算好了地址和数据，从来没有到达。尽管执行不是按顺序的，异常却是精确的。

544ca6846fcf.en: Put together, the pieces make the pipeline that nearly every fast processor has used since the mid-1990s. <bookmark mark='a'/> Fetch, following the branch predictor's guesses. Decode. Rename, through the register alias table and a list of free physical registers. Dispatch, which gives each instruction its slot in the reorder buffer, the issue queue, and, for loads and stores, the load-store queue. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then, out of order: issue, oldest ready instruction first, to an execution unit; execute; and write back, broadcasting the result's tag to everyone waiting for it. <bookmark mark='c'/> And commit, in order, from the head of the reorder buffer. <bookmark mark='d'/> There are two ways to keep the values. Our core, like Intel's Pentium Pro of 1995, keeps each result in its reorder-buffer entry and copies it to the architectural registers at commit. The MIPS R10000 and the Alpha 21264, and most designs since, keep every value in one large physical register file and let the table of names do all the work: commit just declares a mapping final, and frees the register that held the old value.
544ca6846fcf.zh: 把这些部件拼在一起，就是二十世纪九十年代中期以来几乎每个快速处理器都在用的流水线。<bookmark mark='a'/>取指，跟着分支预测器的猜测走。译码。重命名，经过寄存器别名表和一张空闲物理寄存器列表。分派，给每条指令在重排序缓冲区、发射队列里分配位置，取数和存数还要在取数存数队列里分配一项。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后是乱序的部分：发射，最老的就绪指令先走，送到一个执行部件；执行；写回，把结果的标签广播给所有等着它的指令。<bookmark mark='c'/>最后是提交，按顺序，从重排序缓冲区的头部进行。<bookmark mark='d'/>保存值有两种办法。我们的核，像英特尔 1995 年的 Pentium Pro 一样，把每个结果放在它的重排序缓冲区项里，提交时再复制到体系结构寄存器。MIPS R10000 和 Alpha 21264，以及此后的大多数设计，把所有值放在一个大的物理寄存器堆里，让名字表做全部的工作：提交只是宣布一个映射最终生效，并释放保存旧值的那个寄存器。

689bb6a06aa8.en: This core is not a diagram; it is a program, about seven hundred lines, that simulates the machine cycle by cycle. <bookmark mark='a'/> It is checked the way every part of Pebble is checked: on a hundred twenty random programs, in six different configurations, and on the Job, it must finish with exactly the registers, memory, output and instruction count that the emulator gives. <bookmark mark='b'/> And the awkward cases have their own tests: the divide by zero, the store that must never reach memory, the load that must wait. <bookmark mark='c'/> One more property will matter later. The core computes every value for real, including on wrong paths that are later thrown away. Those wrong paths really load from memory. Remember that when we reach chapter nine.
689bb6a06aa8.zh: 这个核不是一张示意图；它是一个程序，大约七百行，一个周期一个周期地模拟这台机器。<bookmark mark='a'/>它的检验方式和 Pebble 的每个部件一样：在一百二十个随机程序上，用六种不同的配置，再加上任务，它结束时的寄存器、存储器、输出和指令条数都必须和仿真器给出的完全一致。<bookmark mark='b'/>那些棘手的情形各有自己的测试：除以零，绝不能到达存储器的存数，必须等待的取数。<bookmark mark='c'/>还有一个性质以后会很重要。这个核真的计算每一个值，包括在后来被扔掉的错误路径上。那些错误路径真的会从存储器取数。到第九章时请记住这一点。

fa716bb495a4.en: Chapter six. Wider, and the wall.
fa716bb495a4.zh: 第六章。更宽，以及那堵墙。

e9368fcf8510.en: In 1991 David Wall, at Digital's research lab, asked how much parallelism real programs contain. Earlier studies had found less than two instructions per cycle inside a basic block, but dozens, by Riseman and Foster's count in 1972, if a machine could see through every branch. Wall's method was the oracle we met in chapter two: record a program's run, schedule every instruction as early as its dependences allow, then take the oracle's powers away one at a time. We repeat it on the Job. <bookmark mark='a'/> With every power: two thousand four hundred instructions a cycle. <bookmark mark='b'/> Without renaming: three point seven. <bookmark mark='c'/> With renaming, but making every load wait until every earlier store's address is known: sixty-two. Memory ordering costs a lot, but not everything. <bookmark mark='d'/> And now keep renaming and perfect memory, but replace the oracle's knowledge of branches with Part 7's tournament predictor, so that each wrong guess blocks everything after it until it is resolved: three point four. <bookmark mark='e'/> With no guessing at all, stopping at every branch: under one half.
e9368fcf8510.zh: 1991 年，数字设备公司研究实验室的大卫·沃尔问：真实的程序里有多少并行性？更早的研究发现，基本块内部每周期不到两条指令，但如果机器能看穿每个分支，按里斯曼和福斯特 1972 年的统计就有几十条。沃尔的方法正是我们在第二章见过的先知：记录一个程序的运行，把每条指令安排在依赖允许的最早时刻，然后一次拿走先知的一种能力。我们在任务上重复这个研究。<bookmark mark='a'/>拥有全部能力时：每周期两千四百条指令。<bookmark mark='b'/>没有重命名：三点七。<bookmark mark='c'/>有重命名，但让每次取数都等到所有更早的存数地址都已知：六十二。存储器顺序代价很大，但不是一切。<bookmark mark='d'/>现在保留重命名和完美的存储器，但把先知对分支的知识换成第7部分的锦标赛预测器，于是每次猜错都会挡住它后面的一切，直到它被解决：三点四。<bookmark mark='e'/>完全不猜，在每个分支前停下：不到二分之一。

c244fa8e1366.en: Now give the oracle real limits: a width, and a window, the number of instructions ahead of the oldest unfinished one that it may look at. A reorder buffer is exactly such a window. <bookmark mark='a'/> With the real predictor, here is instructions per cycle against width, for windows from thirty-two instructions to infinity. The curves lie on top of each other. They climb to about three point three at eight wide and stop. A bigger window is useless, because the machine never gets far ahead before a wrong guess knocks it back. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now make the branches perfect. With a window of one hundred twenty-eight, the curve keeps climbing, to eight. <bookmark mark='c'/> With a window of two thousand and forty-eight, to thirty. The parallelism is there; it is the branches that hide it.
c244fa8e1366.zh: 现在给先知真实的限制：一个宽度，和一个窗口，也就是它可以越过最老的未完成指令向前看多少条。重排序缓冲区正是这样一个窗口。<bookmark mark='a'/>用真实的预测器，这是每周期指令数随宽度的变化，窗口从三十二条到无穷大。这些曲线叠在一起。它们在八条宽时爬到大约三点三，然后停住。更大的窗口没有用，因为机器还没走远，一次猜错就把它打了回来。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在让分支完美。窗口为一百二十八时，曲线继续往上，到八。<bookmark mark='c'/>窗口为两千零四十八时，到三十。并行性就在那里；是分支把它藏了起来。

24d8353304d2.en: Our real core tells the same story. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each cell is the Job's instructions per cycle, for a width and a reorder-buffer size. Going from one to two to four wide helps a lot: zero point eight six, one point two four, one point eight nine. Eight wide adds almost nothing. <bookmark mark='b'/> And across each row, the buffer size changes nothing at all beyond thirty-two entries. Remember the hook: the buffer held about eleven instructions on average. <bookmark mark='c'/> With perfect prediction the same core reaches three point one six at four wide and three point five at eight. What stops it there is the front end and the memory ports: it fetches past at most one taken branch a cycle, and the scan loop takes a jump every six instructions.
24d8353304d2.zh: 我们真实的核讲的是同一个故事。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个格子是任务在某个宽度和某个重排序缓冲区大小下的每周期指令数。从一条宽到两条再到四条帮助很大：零点八六、一点二四、一点八九。八条宽几乎什么也没多。<bookmark mark='b'/>沿着每一行，缓冲区超过三十二项之后大小毫无影响。还记得开头：缓冲区平均只装着大约十一条指令。<bookmark mark='c'/>完美预测时，同一个核在四条宽时达到三点一六，在八条宽时达到三点五。挡住它的是前端和访存端口：它每个周期最多取过一个跳转的分支，而扫描循环每六条指令就有一次跳转。

a855c1a2ae74.en: This is the instruction-level parallelism wall. <bookmark mark='a'/> The parallelism is real: in the Job, thousands of instructions could run at once. <bookmark mark='b'/> But a machine can only exploit what lies within the stretch of program it can predict correctly, and with real branch prediction that stretch is short. <bookmark mark='c'/> Meanwhile each extra unit of width costs more than the last: every new instruction must compare its sources with every other instruction renamed in the same cycle, and every result must be broadcast to every waiting station. <bookmark mark='d'/> So, in the 2000s, designers stopped near four to eight wide and spent their transistors on more cores instead. That is Part 10. But first, the prediction itself: how a machine runs a hundred instructions ahead on a guess.
a855c1a2ae74.zh: 这就是指令级并行之墙。<bookmark mark='a'/>并行性是真实的：在任务里，成千上万条指令本可以同时执行。<bookmark mark='b'/>但机器只能利用它能正确预测的那段程序里的并行性，而用真实的分支预测，这一段很短。<bookmark mark='c'/>同时，每多一点宽度，代价都比上一点更大：每条新指令必须把它的源操作数和同一周期重命名的所有其他指令比较，每个结果都必须广播给每个等待中的保留站。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以在二十一世纪头十年，设计者在四到八条宽附近停了下来，把晶体管花在更多的核上。那是第10部分。但首先是预测本身：一台机器怎样凭一个猜测跑到一百条指令之前。

bb87d9f1bdbd.en: Part 7's pipeline guessed branches so that fetch never had to wait. The reorder buffer turns that small trick into a large one. <bookmark mark='a'/> The predictor guesses every branch, and fetch follows the guess. <bookmark mark='b'/> Everything after the branch is renamed and executed as usual. It is speculative: done on the strength of a guess. <bookmark mark='c'/> The reorder buffer makes this safe, because nothing can commit past a branch that has not been resolved. All speculative work stays in the buffer, unofficial. <bookmark mark='d'/> When the branch finally executes, either the guess was right, and there is nothing to do, or it was wrong: then every younger instruction is dropped, the register alias table is put back as it was at the branch, and fetching restarts at the correct target. Real cores take a snapshot of the alias table at every branch, so the repair takes a single cycle.
bb87d9f1bdbd.zh: 第7部分的流水线猜测分支，好让取指永远不必等待。重排序缓冲区把这个小把戏变成了大把戏。<bookmark mark='a'/>预测器猜测每一个分支，取指跟着猜测走。<bookmark mark='b'/>分支之后的一切照常重命名和执行。这些是推测执行的：凭一个猜测做下的事。<bookmark mark='c'/>重排序缓冲区让这件事安全，因为没有指令能越过一个尚未解决的分支提交。所有推测的工作都留在缓冲区里，不算数。<bookmark mark='d'/>分支终于执行时，要么猜对了，什么也不用做；要么猜错了：那么每条更年轻的指令都被丢弃，寄存器别名表恢复成分支时的样子，取指从正确的目标重新开始。真实的核在每个分支处给别名表拍一张快照，所以修复只要一个周期。

c0968545aedc.en: Here is one, from the core running the Job. Each bar starts when the instruction was fetched; grey is fetch and decode. <bookmark mark='a'/> This is the scan loop's branch on the entry's length. The predictor guessed that the lengths matched, so fetch went on into the letter-comparing code. <bookmark mark='b'/> Eleven instructions down the wrong path were fetched, renamed, and some even executed. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then the branch executed and found the lengths were different. Everything after it was dropped, struck through here; none of it had committed, so none of it counts. <bookmark mark='d'/> Fetch restarted at the right place, and the next instructions arrived about eight cycles after the branch itself had. Those eight cycles, the misprediction penalty, are the price of a wrong guess: in today's deep cores, about fifteen to twenty.
c0968545aedc.zh: 这是一次，来自运行任务的处理器核。每根条从指令被取进来时开始；灰色是取指和译码。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是扫描循环里检查表项长度的分支。预测器猜长度相同，于是取指继续进入比较字母的代码。<bookmark mark='b'/>错误路径上的十一条指令被取进、重命名，有些甚至已经执行。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后分支执行，发现长度不同。它后面的一切都被丢弃，在这里被划掉；它们都还没提交，所以都不算数。<bookmark mark='d'/>取指在正确的地方重新开始，接下来的指令比分支本身晚了大约八个周期到达。这八个周期，也就是预测错误的代价，是一次猜错的价格：在今天的深流水线核里，大约是十五到二十个周期。

b222f233949b.en: How much does the guessing matter? Run the Job's first chapter on the same core with four predictors. <bookmark mark='a'/> Guess every branch taken, and the core manages zero point six nine instructions per cycle: worse than the in-order pipeline. <bookmark mark='b'/> A two-bit counter: one point eight seven. The tournament: one point eight nine. <bookmark mark='c'/> A perfect predictor: three point one six. The branches cost the core forty percent of its speed. <bookmark mark='d'/> With the tournament predictor, twenty-two thousand wrong guesses threw away two hundred fifty thousand instructions: thirty percent more work than the program needed, all of it wasted. Including twenty-nine thousand loads, on paths the program never took. Hold on to that number.
b222f233949b.zh: 猜测有多重要？在同一个核上用四种预测器运行任务第一章。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个分支都猜跳转，核只有每周期零点六九条指令：比按顺序的流水线还差。<bookmark mark='b'/>两位计数器：一点八七。锦标赛预测器：一点八九。<bookmark mark='c'/>完美预测器：三点一六。分支让这个核损失了百分之四十的速度。<bookmark mark='d'/>用锦标赛预测器时，两万两千次猜错扔掉了二十五万条指令：比程序需要的多出百分之三十的工作，全部白做。其中包括两万九千次取数，发生在程序从未走过的路径上。记住这个数字。

a84c9f767d76.en: Two lines of arithmetic explain the empty window from the hook. <bookmark mark='a'/> The chapter has eight hundred twenty-seven thousand instructions and twenty-two thousand wrong guesses: one every thirty-seven instructions. However large the window, the machine can only ever be about thirty-seven instructions ahead on the right path before it is thrown back. <bookmark mark='b'/> And the cost of each throw: the time per instruction is what it would be with perfect prediction, plus the rate of wrong guesses times a penalty P. <bookmark mark='c'/> Put in the measured numbers, and the penalty comes out at about eight cycles, just what the recording showed. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the window fills for a few dozen instructions, then drains, again and again. Better prediction is worth more than a bigger window, and that is why real cores spend so much on predictors.
a84c9f767d76.zh: 两行算术就能解释开头那个空荡荡的窗口。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一章有八十二万七千条指令和两万两千次猜错：每三十七条指令一次。不管窗口多大，机器在正确的路径上最多只能领先大约三十七条指令，然后就被打回去。<bookmark mark='b'/>每次被打回去的代价：每条指令的时间等于完美预测时的时间，加上猜错的频率乘以代价 P。<bookmark mark='c'/>代入测得的数字，代价大约是八个周期，正是录下来的那一次显示的。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以窗口装进几十条指令，然后清空，一遍又一遍。更好的预测比更大的窗口更值钱，这就是为什么真实的核在预测器上花这么多。

a94d52503631.en: Chapter eight. Loads, stores, and their order.
a94d52503631.zh: 第八章。取数、存数与它们的顺序。

1833e22564de.en: Renaming removed the false dependences between registers, because a register's name is right there in the instruction, and can be checked as soon as it is decoded. Memory is harder. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here a store writes to an address in a3, which is still being computed, and a load right after it reads from s0 plus four, which is already known. <bookmark mark='b'/> If the two addresses are the same, the load must wait for the store and take the store's value. <bookmark mark='c'/> If they are different, the load could go at once. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the machine cannot tell which, until the store's address is known. Dependences through memory are hidden behind arithmetic.
1833e22564de.zh: 重命名消除了寄存器之间的假依赖，因为寄存器的名字就写在指令里，一译码就能检查。存储器难得多。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里一条存数写到 a3 里的地址，而 a3 还在计算中；紧跟着的一条取数从 s0 加四读，这个地址已经知道了。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果两个地址相同，取数必须等存数，并取走存数的值。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果不同，取数可以马上走。<bookmark mark='d'/>而在存数的地址算出来之前，机器无法知道是哪一种。经过存储器的依赖藏在算术后面。

7599782ca45d.en: So a core keeps its memory operations in two queues, in program order. <bookmark mark='a'/> Stores wait in the store queue until they commit; only then do they write memory, so a store on a wrong path never touches it. <bookmark mark='b'/> A load, when it executes, searches the older stores. If the youngest older store to the same address has its data, the load takes the value straight from the queue: store-to-load forwarding. <bookmark mark='c'/> The hard case is the first entry, a store whose address is unknown. There are three policies. Wait, conservatively, while any older store's address is unknown. Or speculate: go ahead, and check later. Or do what the Alpha 21264 did in 1998: speculate, but remember the loads that have been caught out before, and make only those wait.
7599782ca45d.zh: 所以处理器核把它的访存操作按程序顺序放在两个队列里。<bookmark mark='a'/>存数在存数队列里等到提交；只有那时才写存储器，所以错误路径上的存数永远碰不到它。<bookmark mark='b'/>取数执行时，搜索更老的存数。如果对同一地址的最年轻的更老存数已经有了数据，取数直接从队列里拿走这个值：存数到取数转发。<bookmark mark='c'/>难办的是第一项，一条地址未知的存数。有三种策略。保守地等，只要有更老的存数地址未知就等。或者推测：先走，以后再检查。或者像 1998 年的Alpha 21264 那样：推测，但记住以前被抓到过的那些取数，只让它们等。

a42e404506f1.en: Here is speculation caught out, on our core. A divide produces the store's address offset, so the store cannot compute its address for sixteen cycles. <bookmark mark='a'/> The load after it, whose address is known, does not wait. It reads its word from memory at once, and gets zero. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sixteen cycles later the store's address arrives, and the store queue checks every younger load that has already run. One of them read the very word this store writes. <bookmark mark='c'/> That load's value is wrong, and so is anything computed from it. So the load and everything after it are squashed and fetched again, exactly as after a wrong branch. <bookmark mark='d'/> The second time, the store has committed, and the load reads seventy-seven. Here the gamble lost, and cost six cycles.
a42e404506f1.zh: 这是在我们的核上被抓到的一次推测。一次除法产生存数地址的偏移量，所以存数在十六个周期里算不出它的地址。<bookmark mark='a'/>后面那条地址已知的取数不等。它立刻从存储器读出它的字，得到零。<bookmark mark='b'/>十六个周期后，存数的地址到了，存数队列检查每一条已经执行过的更年轻的取数。其中一条读的正是这条存数要写的字。<bookmark mark='c'/>那条取数的值是错的，用它算出的一切也是错的。所以这条取数和它后面的一切都被清除，重新取进来，和分支猜错之后一模一样。<bookmark mark='d'/>第二次，存数已经提交，取数读到七十七。这一次赌输了，代价是六个周期。

2820bea963e2.en: When does it matter? Here is a loop that counts samples into buckets, where every sample misses the cache. <bookmark mark='a'/> The store at the bottom writes a count whose address depends on the sample, so its address is unknown for sixty cycles. The next trip's sample load, which has nothing to do with the counts, comes right after it. <bookmark mark='b'/> A conservative machine makes every load wait for that store's address: each miss in turn, ninety-eight thousand cycles for fifteen hundred samples. <bookmark mark='c'/> A speculative machine lets the sample loads run ahead, so a dozen misses overlap: seven and a half thousand cycles. Twenty-three times, two count loads collided with stores to the same bucket, and had to be redone. <bookmark mark='d'/> The wait table learns, after one collision, that the count load is the risky one, and makes only it wait, while the sample loads still run ahead. Thirteen times faster than waiting. Real cores predict memory dependences in just this way; Intel's count each recovery from a wrong guess as a machine clear, a number any programmer can read from the performance counters.
2820bea963e2.zh: 什么时候这件事要紧？这是一个把样本计数到桶里的循环，每个样本都会缓存缺失。<bookmark mark='a'/>底部的存数写一个计数，它的地址取决于样本，所以六十个周期里地址都未知。下一趟的样本取数和计数毫无关系，却紧跟在它后面。<bookmark mark='b'/>保守的机器让每次取数都等这条存数的地址：缺失一个接一个，一千五百个样本用九万八千个周期。<bookmark mark='c'/>推测的机器让样本取数先跑，于是十几次缺失重叠在一起：七千五百个周期。有二十三次，两次计数取数和写同一个桶的存数撞上了，只好重做。<bookmark mark='d'/>等待表在撞过一次之后就学会，计数取数才是有风险的那个，只让它等，样本取数照样先跑。比一直等快十三倍。真实的核正是这样预测存储器依赖的；英特尔的核把每次从错误猜测中恢复记为一次机器清除，任何程序员都可以从性能计数器里读到这个数。

a7dc510ac4f9.en: And on the Job? <bookmark mark='a'/> All three policies give exactly the same cycle count. <bookmark mark='b'/> The Job does a hundred fifty-five thousand loads in its first chapter but only five thousand stores, one or two each time it counts a word, and their addresses are known early. There is nothing to wait for. A machine's features earn their keep on some programs and sit idle on others, which is why architects measure on many.
a7dc510ac4f9.zh: 那么任务呢？<bookmark mark='a'/>三种策略给出完全相同的周期数。<bookmark mark='b'/>任务在第一章里做了十五万五千次取数，但只有五千次存数，每数一个词一两次，而且它们的地址很早就知道了。没有什么可等的。机器的一项特性在某些程序上物有所值，在另一些程序上闲着，这就是为什么设计者要在许多程序上测量。

2867987e3d7b.en: Before the attack, the channel it uses. Part 9 will build caches properly; for now, one fact. A read that finds its data in the cache takes two cycles on our core; one that must go to memory takes sixty. <bookmark mark='a'/> Lay out a probe array: two hundred fifty-six cache lines, one for each possible value of a byte. Flush them all from the cache. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now let some other code run, and suppose it reads line eleven. <bookmark mark='c'/> Afterwards, time a read of every line. Two hundred fifty-five of them take sixty cycles. One takes two. <bookmark mark='d'/> The timing reveals which line was touched, and so which byte value the other code used, though nobody told us. This is Flush plus Reload, described by Yuval Yarom and Katrina Falkner in 2014. Timing attacks on caches go back further: in 2005 they were used to steal encryption keys.
2867987e3d7b.zh: 在讲攻击之前，先讲它用的信道。第9部分会好好地造缓存；现在只需要一个事实。在我们的核上，一次在缓存里找到数据的读要两个周期；一次必须去存储器的读要六十个周期。<bookmark mark='a'/>摆出一个探测数组：两百五十六个缓存行，每个可能的字节值一行。把它们全部从缓存里冲掉。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在让另一段代码运行，假设它读了第十一行。<bookmark mark='c'/>之后，给每一行的读取计时。两百五十五行要六十个周期。有一行只要两个。<bookmark mark='d'/>计时暴露了哪一行被碰过，因而暴露了另一段代码用的是哪个字节值，尽管没有人告诉我们。这就是冲刷加重载，由约瓦尔·亚罗姆和卡特里娜·福克纳在 2014 年描述。针对缓存的计时攻击还要更早：2005 年它们就被用来窃取加密密钥。

817aff14e149.en: Now the victim. It is the most ordinary code in the world: a bounds check. <bookmark mark='a'/> If x is less than the size of array one, read array one at x, and use the byte to index another array. <bookmark mark='b'/> In Pebble's instructions: load the size, compare, and only if x is in bounds, load the byte and then the probe line it selects. <bookmark mark='c'/> Just past the end of array one, in the same address space, sits a secret: here, six letters. The bounds check is exactly what stops anyone calling this code from reading them. Architecturally, it is perfect: run it on the emulator with any x, and it never touches the secret.
817aff14e149.zh: 现在是受害者。它是世界上最普通的代码：一次边界检查。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果 x 小于数组一的大小，就读出数组一的第 x 个字节，再用这个字节去索引另一个数组。<bookmark mark='b'/>用 Pebble 的指令写：取出大小，比较，只有当 x 在界内时，才取出那个字节，再取出它选中的探测行。<bookmark mark='c'/>紧挨着数组一的末尾，在同一个地址空间里，放着一个秘密：这里是六个字母。边界检查正是阻止调用者读到它们的东西。从体系结构上看，它无懈可击：在仿真器上用任何 x 运行它，它都从不碰那个秘密。

39a8ae4d0c6d.en: Here is the attack, as it runs on our out-of-order core. <bookmark mark='a'/> First, train the branch predictor: call the victim six times with x in bounds, so the bounds check learns to expect in bounds. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then flush the probe lines from the cache, and flush array one's size as well. Our core has a model instruction for that, like x86's flush instruction. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now call the victim with x equal to sixteen, past the end. The load of the size misses: sixty cycles before the comparison can run. The predictor guesses in bounds, as it was trained to. So for sixty cycles the core runs ahead, speculatively: it loads array one at sixteen, which is the secret letter P, shifts it, and loads the probe line P times sixty-four. That load misses too, and brings the line into the cache. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then the size arrives, the comparison fails, and the core squashes everything after the branch. Registers go back to how they were. As far as the program can tell, the secret was never read. But the probe line is still in the cache.
39a8ae4d0c6d.zh: 这就是在我们的乱序核上运行的攻击。<bookmark mark='a'/>首先，训练分支预测器：用界内的 x 调用受害者六次，让边界检查学会预期在界内。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后把探测行从缓存里冲掉，连数组一的大小也冲掉。我们的核有一条模型指令做这件事，就像 x86 的冲刷指令。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在用等于十六的 x 调用受害者，越过了末尾。取大小的操作缺失：比较还要六十个周期才能执行。预测器照它被训练的那样，猜在界内。于是在这六十个周期里，核推测地往前跑：它取出数组一的第十六个字节，也就是秘密的字母 P，移位，再取出第 P 乘六十四号探测行。这次取数也缺失了，把那一行带进了缓存。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后大小到了，比较失败，核清除了分支之后的一切。寄存器恢复原样。就程序所能知道的而言，秘密从来没有被读过。但那条探测行仍然在缓存里。

b931cb478acc.en: Now the attacker times a read of every probe line, using the cycle counter. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are the times our core measured in the first round. Two hundred fifty-four lines take sixty-three cycles: memory. <bookmark mark='b'/> One takes five: line eighty, which is the code of the letter P. <bookmark mark='c'/> Repeat with x equal to seventeen, eighteen, and so on, one round per byte. In a hundred nine thousand cycles, the attack prints the secret, letter by letter. A program that the bounds check should have stopped has read memory it was never allowed to read, through instructions that, architecturally, never ran.
b931cb478acc.zh: 现在攻击者用周期计数器给每一条探测行的读取计时。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是我们的核在第一轮测得的时间。两百五十四行要六十三个周期：存储器。<bookmark mark='b'/>有一行只要五个：第八十行，正是字母 P 的编码。<bookmark mark='c'/>让 x 等于十七、十八，依此类推，每个字节一轮。在十万九千个周期里，攻击一个字母一个字母地打印出秘密。一个本应被边界检查挡住的程序，读到了它永远不该读的存储器，而且是通过一些在体系结构上从未执行过的指令。

782a5600ba38.en: There are two classic fixes, and our core can measure both. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first is a speculation barrier after the check: an instruction that nothing younger may pass until it commits. On x86 it is l-fence; on our core, a read of the cycle counter. <bookmark mark='b'/> The second is cleverer. Compute, without any branch, a mask that is all ones if x is in bounds and zero if not, and and it into x. On a wrong path the index becomes zero, which reads nothing secret. Linux does exactly this, in a macro called array index no spec. <bookmark mark='c'/> Both stop the leak: the probe shows no fast line. <bookmark mark='d'/> But look at the price. Called in a loop, the victim costs four cycles a call. With the barrier, twelve: the barrier stops all overlap, not only the dangerous kind. With the mask, five. <bookmark mark='e'/> The mask blocks only the value that could leak, so it is what kernels use where they can, and it must be written by hand, at every bounds check that matters.
782a5600ba38.zh: 有两种经典的修复，我们的核都能测量。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一种是在检查之后放一道推测屏障：一条在它提交之前任何更年轻的指令都不能越过的指令。在 x86 上它是 lfence；在我们的核上，是读一次周期计数器。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二种更巧妙。不用任何分支，算出一个掩码：x 在界内时全为一，否则为零，再把它和 x 做与运算。在错误路径上，下标变成零，读不到任何秘密。Linux 正是这样做的，用一个叫 array_index_nospec 的宏。<bookmark mark='c'/>两种都挡住了泄露：探测显示没有快的那一行。<bookmark mark='d'/>但看看代价。在循环里调用，受害者每次调用花四个周期。加上屏障，十二个：屏障阻止了一切重叠，而不只是危险的那种。加上掩码，五个。<bookmark mark='e'/>掩码只挡住可能泄露的那个值，所以内核在能用的地方用它，而且必须手工写在每一个要紧的边界检查上。

1c3c4f33c36d.en: This is the attack published in January 2018 as Spectre, found independently by Paul Kocher and colleagues and by Jann Horn of Google's Project Zero, together with a second variant that mistrains indirect branches instead. <bookmark mark='a'/> Published with it was Meltdown, by Moritz Lipp and others: on many Intel cores a load from kernel memory, which should have faulted, passed its value to the instructions after it before the fault took effect, so any program could read the kernel. <bookmark mark='b'/> The fixes came at every level. Operating systems gave the kernel its own page tables. Compilers learned new ways to make indirect calls. Browsers made their timers coarser and put each site in its own process. Chips were redesigned. <bookmark mark='c'/> Meltdown was a bug in some designs. Spectre is not a bug at all: it is what speculation does, and out-of-order cores from Intel, AMD, Arm and IBM were all affected. Part 55 returns to it. The Frontier chapter asks whether speculation can be made safe.
1c3c4f33c36d.zh: 这就是 2018 年 1 月以幽灵之名公布的攻击，由保罗·科赫及其同事和谷歌零号项目的扬·霍恩各自独立发现，同时公布的还有另一个变种，它改为误训间接分支。<bookmark mark='a'/>与它一起公布的是熔断，由莫里茨·利普等人发现：在许多英特尔核上，一次从内核存储器的取数本应出错，却在错误生效之前就把它的值传给了后面的指令，于是任何程序都能读内核。<bookmark mark='b'/>修复出现在每一个层次上。操作系统给内核单独的页表。编译器学会了新的间接调用写法。浏览器把计时器变粗，并把每个网站放进单独的进程。芯片被重新设计。<bookmark mark='c'/>熔断是某些设计里的缺陷。幽灵根本不是缺陷：它就是推测执行本身会做的事，英特尔、AMD、Arm 和 IBM 的乱序核都受到了影响。第55部分会回到它。前沿一章会问：推测执行能不能变得安全。

95c111fe5111.zh: 第十章。编译器的另一条路。

48932dadbe68.en: Everything we have built so far finds parallelism at run time, in hardware, and that hardware is costly. <bookmark mark='a'/> Renaming W instructions in one cycle means comparing each one's sources with the destinations of all the others renamed alongside it: work that grows as the square of the width. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every result's tag must be compared with every operand waiting in the issue queue. <bookmark mark='c'/> And every cycle, the oldest ready instructions must be picked out of dozens, in a fraction of a nanosecond. <bookmark mark='d'/> So from the early 1980s, Joseph Fisher at Yale and others argued for the opposite design. Let the compiler, which can study the whole program at leisure, find the independent operations and pack them into one very long instruction word, a bundle with one slot for each unit. The hardware then needs no scheduling at all.
48932dadbe68.zh: 到目前为止我们造的一切都在运行时、用硬件寻找并行性，而这样的硬件很贵。<bookmark mark='a'/>在一个周期里重命名 W 条指令，意味着把每条指令的源操作数和同时重命名的所有其他指令的目的寄存器比较：工作量随宽度的平方增长。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个结果的标签都必须和发射队列里每个等待中的操作数比较。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且每个周期都要在几分之一纳秒里从几十条指令中挑出最老的就绪指令。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以从二十世纪八十年代初起，耶鲁的约瑟夫·费希尔等人主张相反的设计。让编译器，它可以从容地研究整个程序，找出相互独立的操作，把它们打包进一个超长指令字，一个为每个部件留一个槽的指令束。这样硬件就完全不需要调度。

43fab8b1c25b.en: Here is the Job's scan loop, compiled for a four-wide VLIW machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first bundle holds four operations that need nothing from each other: the end-of-table test, the load of the entry's length, and the two increments, which may share a bundle with the instructions reading the old values. <bookmark mark='b'/> The second bundle is empty. The compiler knows a load takes two cycles, and nothing else in this trip is ready, so it must fill the slots with no-ops. <bookmark mark='c'/> The third holds the length test and the jump back. Three cycles a trip, against the pipeline's seven, with no scheduling hardware at all. But half the slots are wasted.
43fab8b1c25b.zh: 这是为一台四槽超长指令字机器编译的任务扫描循环。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一个指令束装着四个互不依赖的操作：表尾检查、取表项长度，以及两次递增；递增可以和读旧值的指令放在同一个束里。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二个指令束是空的。编译器知道取数要两个周期，这一趟里没有别的就绪，所以只能用空操作填满这些槽。<bookmark mark='c'/>第三个装着长度检查和跳回。一趟三个周期，而流水线要七个，而且完全没有调度硬件。但一半的槽浪费了。

f847dff85530.en: A compiler can do better, by overlapping trips: software pipelining, worked out by Bob Rau and others around 1981, and by Monica Lam in 1988. <bookmark mark='a'/> Start a new trip every two cycles. Trip two begins while trip one is still finishing, in the slots trip one leaves free, and so on: in the steady state each bundle mixes the start of one trip with the end of the one before. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two cycles is as fast as this loop can go on four slots. The interval between trips is bounded by the resources, six operations into four slots, and by the loop-carried chain, the add to t0, which needs one cycle. The larger bound wins: two. That is three instructions a cycle on the loop's common path, with none of the out-of-order hardware. Part 13's compiler will do this kind of scheduling.
f847dff85530.zh: 编译器还能做得更好，办法是让各趟重叠：软件流水，由鲍勃·劳等人在 1981 年前后、莫妮卡·林在 1988 年发展起来。<bookmark mark='a'/>每两个周期开始新的一趟。第二趟在第一趟还没结束时就开始，用第一趟留下的空槽，依此类推：在稳定状态下，每个指令束把一趟的开头和前一趟的结尾混在一起。<bookmark mark='b'/>两个周期是这个循环在四个槽上能达到的最快速度。两趟之间的间隔受资源约束，六个操作装进四个槽，也受循环携带的那条链约束，就是对 t0 的加法，它需要一个周期。较大的那个界胜出：二。这是在循环的常见路径上每周期三条指令，完全不需要乱序硬件。第13部分的编译器会做这种调度。

c1b63d099c4e.en: Then why does your laptop not work this way? <bookmark mark='a'/> Because the compiler must plan for latencies it cannot know. It assumed a load takes two cycles. When a load misses the cache and takes sixty, a VLIW machine, marching in lockstep, stalls every slot of every bundle behind it, which is exactly the in-order problem of the hook. The out-of-order core simply finds other work. <bookmark mark='b'/> It also cannot know branches that depend on data, like our length test, so it must guess at compile time, or execute both sides under predicates and throw one away. <bookmark mark='c'/> And code scheduled for one width and one set of latencies is wrong for the next generation of chips. <bookmark mark='d'/> Intel and Hewlett-Packard bet heavily on this design, as EPIC, in the Itanium of 2001, with features to soften each problem. It arrived late, and in 2003 AMD's sixty-four-bit x86 ran existing software fast; the last Itaniums shipped in 2021. <bookmark mark='e'/> VLIW lives on where programs are known and latencies fixed: in digital signal processors, and in some machine-learning accelerators.
c1b63d099c4e.zh: 那为什么你的笔记本电脑不是这样工作的？<bookmark mark='a'/>因为编译器必须为它不可能知道的延迟做计划。它假设一次取数要两个周期。当一次取数缓存缺失、要六十个周期时，一台步调一致前进的超长指令字机器会让它后面每个指令束的每个槽都停下，这正是开头那个按顺序执行的问题。乱序核则只是去找别的事做。<bookmark mark='b'/>它也不可能知道依赖数据的分支，比如我们的长度检查，所以只能在编译时猜，或者在谓词控制下把两边都执行，再扔掉一边。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且为一种宽度和一组延迟调度好的代码，对下一代芯片就是错的。<bookmark mark='d'/>英特尔和惠普在这种设计上下了重注，称为 EPIC，在 2001 年的 Itanium 里推出，并加了缓解每个问题的特性。它来得太晚，而 2003 年 AMD 的六十四位 x86 让现有软件跑得飞快；最后一批 Itanium 在 2021 年出货。<bookmark mark='e'/>超长指令字在程序已知、延迟固定的地方活了下来：在数字信号处理器里，以及在一些机器学习加速器里。

abfad968b671.zh: 第十一章。精简与复杂指令集。

f29ba6b2e672.en: Pebble has a reduced instruction set: every instruction does one simple thing, and only loads and stores touch memory. That was once a heresy. <bookmark mark='a'/> Recall the iron law from Part 7: time is instructions, times cycles per instruction, times the clock period. <bookmark mark='b'/> The machines of the 1970s, like Digital's VAX, attacked the first factor. They offered rich instructions, adding memory to memory, even evaluating a polynomial in one instruction, so programs needed fewer of them. Each was run by microcode, a little program inside the processor, and took many cycles. <bookmark mark='c'/> John Cocke at IBM noticed that compilers hardly used the rich instructions. His 801 project, and then David Patterson's RISC at Berkeley and John Hennessy's MIPS at Stanford, attacked the other two factors instead: simple instructions, each one cycle in a pipeline, with a fast clock. More instructions, but each far cheaper. <bookmark mark='d'/> Patterson and Ditzel's paper, The Case for the Reduced Instruction Set Computer, appeared in 1980, and the argument raged for a decade.
f29ba6b2e672.zh: Pebble 用的是精简指令集：每条指令只做一件简单的事，只有取数和存数碰存储器。这曾经是一种异端。<bookmark mark='a'/>回忆第7部分的铁律：时间等于指令条数，乘以每条指令的周期数，乘以时钟周期。<bookmark mark='b'/>二十世纪七十年代的机器，比如数字设备公司的 VAX，攻的是第一个因子。它们提供丰富的指令，从存储器加到存储器，甚至一条指令求一个多项式的值，于是程序需要的指令更少。每条指令由微码，也就是处理器内部的一个小程序来执行，要花许多周期。<bookmark mark='c'/>IBM 的约翰·科克注意到，编译器几乎不用那些丰富的指令。他的 801 项目，以及随后伯克利大卫·帕特森的 RISC 和斯坦福约翰·轩尼诗的 MIPS，转而攻另外两个因子：简单的指令，每条在流水线里一个周期，配上快的时钟。指令更多，但每条便宜得多。<bookmark mark='d'/>帕特森和迪泽尔的论文《精简指令集计算机的理由》发表于 1980 年，这场争论持续了十年。

fe9cd0bf3782.en: What does the Job look like as a RISC program? <bookmark mark='a'/> Over its first chapter: about a third arithmetic, a third branches, a fifth loads, an eighth jumps, and hardly any stores. <bookmark mark='b'/> A CISC machine like x86 can take an operand straight from memory. The scan loop's load of an entry's length, used once by the comparison and then dead, would be part of a single x86 compare. <bookmark mark='c'/> Counting over the whole trace, fifty-nine percent of the Job's loads are used exactly this way, so an x86 version would need about eleven percent fewer instructions. That is the CISC advantage, measured: real, and modest.
fe9cd0bf3782.zh: 作为一个精简指令集程序，任务是什么样子？<bookmark mark='a'/>在它的第一章里：大约三分之一是算术，三分之一是分支，五分之一是取数，八分之一是跳转，存数几乎没有。<bookmark mark='b'/>像 x86 这样的复杂指令集机器可以直接从存储器取操作数。扫描循环里取表项长度的那次取数，只被比较用一次就不再需要，在 x86 里会成为一条比较指令的一部分。<bookmark mark='c'/>在整条轨迹上数一数，任务的取数里有百分之五十九是这样用的，所以 x86 版本大约少需要百分之十一的指令。这就是测出来的复杂指令集优势：真实，而且不大。

ea794f122ebb.en: The argument ended in a merger. <bookmark mark='a'/> Since Intel's Pentium Pro in 1995, x86 processors have translated each instruction, as it is decoded, into simple micro-operations. An add to memory becomes a load, an add, and a store. <bookmark mark='b'/> Everything after the decoder is an out-of-order RISC machine like ours, renaming and scheduling micro-ops. <bookmark mark='c'/> Modern decoders even fuse pairs back together: a compare and the branch on it travel through the core as one. <bookmark mark='d'/> What remains of the old difference is mostly the decoder. x86 instructions range from one byte to fifteen, so finding where each starts, several at a time, is hard work that a fixed-length instruction set never needs.
ea794f122ebb.zh: 这场争论以合并告终。<bookmark mark='a'/>自 1995 年英特尔的 Pentium Pro 起，x86 处理器在译码时把每条指令翻译成简单的微操作。一条加到存储器的加法变成一次取数、一次加法和一次存数。<bookmark mark='b'/>译码器之后的一切都是一台像我们这样的乱序精简指令集机器，对微操作做重命名和调度。<bookmark mark='c'/>现代的译码器甚至把成对的指令重新融合：一次比较和依据它的分支作为一个整体穿过处理器核。<bookmark mark='d'/>旧差别留下来的主要是译码器。x86 指令从一个字节到十五个字节不等，所以一次找出好几条指令各自从哪里开始是件苦差事，而定长指令集根本不需要。

f2227c367a37.en: Where did the instruction sets go? <bookmark mark='a'/> x86 kept the personal computer and the server, carrying every instruction since 1978 for compatibility. <bookmark mark='b'/> Arm, a RISC designed at Acorn in 1985 by Sophie Wilson and Steve Furber, took phones, then tablets, and in 2020 Apple's laptops. <bookmark mark='c'/> RISC-V, begun at Berkeley in 2010, is an open instruction set that anyone may implement without a licence; Pebble's design borrows from it. <bookmark mark='d'/> And in 2017 John Hennessy and David Patterson received the Turing Award, for the quantitative approach to computer design that this whole act follows: measure, then build.
f2227c367a37.zh: 这些指令集后来去了哪里？<bookmark mark='a'/>x86 守住了个人电脑和服务器，为了兼容带着 1978 年以来的每一条指令。<bookmark mark='b'/>Arm，1985 年由索菲·威尔逊和史蒂夫·弗伯在 Acorn 设计的精简指令集，拿下了手机，然后是平板，2020 年又拿下了苹果的笔记本电脑。<bookmark mark='c'/>RISC-V，2010 年始于伯克利，是一个开放的指令集，任何人都可以不经许可地实现它；Pebble 的设计借鉴了它。<bookmark mark='d'/>2017 年，约翰·轩尼诗和大卫·帕特森获得图灵奖，表彰他们对计算机设计的定量方法，这正是整个这一幕所遵循的：先测量，再建造。

fd5cd3d1dde5.en: Chapter six ended with a machine that has more width than one program can use. Here are a four-wide machine's issue slots, four per cycle, over twenty-four cycles of the Job. <bookmark mark='a'/> Filled squares are slots that started an instruction. Some cycles use all four; many use one or two; some none, while a misprediction is repaired. <bookmark mark='b'/> On our real core, the Job reaches one point nine instructions per cycle out of four: more than half the issue slots go unused, cycle after cycle. <bookmark mark='c'/> The hardware is built, powered and waiting. One program simply cannot fill it.
fd5cd3d1dde5.zh: 第六章结束时，我们有一台宽度超过一个程序所能利用的机器。这是一台四槽机器的发射槽，每周期四个，在任务的二十四个周期里。<bookmark mark='a'/>填满的方格是开始了一条指令的槽。有些周期四个都用上了；许多周期用一两个；有些一个也没有，那是在修复一次猜错。<bookmark mark='b'/>在我们真实的核上，任务达到每周期一点九条指令，而上限是四：一半以上的发射槽一个周期又一个周期地空着。<bookmark mark='c'/>硬件已经造好、通了电、在等着。只是一个程序填不满它。

4aecd6dede6d.en: In 1995 Dean Tullsen, Susan Eggers and Henry Levy proposed the obvious, radical fix: let a second program use the same core at the same time. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here the Job runs on two different books, as two threads sharing one four-wide core. Their instructions mix freely in the issue slots, and the second thread fills many of the holes the first one leaves. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each thread needs only its own program counter, its own register alias table, and its own branch history. Everything expensive is shared: the issue queue, the functional units, the caches, and the reorder buffer, split between them. Because renaming keeps the threads' registers apart, the scheduler does not even need to know which instruction belongs to whom. <bookmark mark='c'/> And when one thread guesses a branch wrong, only its own instructions are thrown away; the other thread carries on.
4aecd6dede6d.zh: 1995 年，迪恩·塔尔森、苏珊·埃格斯和亨利·利维提出了一个显而易见又激进的办法：让第二个程序同时使用同一个核。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里任务在两本不同的书上运行，作为两个线程共用一个四槽核。它们的指令在发射槽里自由混合，第二个线程填上了第一个留下的许多空洞。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个线程只需要自己的程序计数器、自己的寄存器别名表和自己的分支历史。所有昂贵的东西都是共用的：发射队列、功能部件、缓存，以及在两者之间分开的重排序缓冲区。因为重命名把两个线程的寄存器分开了，调度器甚至不需要知道哪条指令属于谁。<bookmark mark='c'/>当一个线程猜错分支时，只有它自己的指令被扔掉；另一个线程继续执行。

5ed3693f68df.en: How much does it help? The oracle scheduler with real branch prediction can answer. <bookmark mark='a'/> Four wide, with a window of a hundred twenty-eight: one thread manages two point seven instructions per cycle; two threads, each with half the window, three point seven together, forty percent more. <bookmark mark='b'/> Eight wide, with a window of two hundred fifty-six, the gain is eighty percent: the wider the machine, the more a single thread wastes, and the more a second thread recovers. <bookmark mark='c'/> Intel shipped two-thread SMT as Hyper-Threading in 2002, IBM in the POWER5 in 2004, and IBM's POWER8 runs eight threads per core. The price is that each thread runs slower than it would alone, and that threads sharing a core can watch each other: one can time its own use of the units to learn what the other is doing. After 2018 some systems turned SMT off for exactly that reason.
5ed3693f68df.zh: 它能帮多少？用带真实分支预测的先知调度器就能回答。<bookmark mark='a'/>四条宽、窗口一百二十八：一个线程每周期两点七条指令；两个线程，各用一半窗口，合起来三点七，多出百分之四十。<bookmark mark='b'/>八条宽、窗口二百五十六，提升是百分之八十：机器越宽，单个线程浪费得越多，第二个线程收回得越多。<bookmark mark='c'/>英特尔在2002 年以超线程之名推出双线程的同时多线程，IBM 在 2004 年的 POWER5 里推出，IBM 的 POWER8 每个核跑八个线程。代价是每个线程都比单独运行时慢，而且共用一个核的线程可以互相窥视：一个线程可以给自己使用部件的时间计时，从而得知另一个在做什么。2018 年之后，有些系统正是因为这个原因关掉了同时多线程。

bdcf77415f40.en: Chapter thirteen. Modern cores in numbers.
bdcf77415f40.zh: 第十三章。用数字看现代处理器核。

735d24470fef.en: How far have real machines taken all this? Here is the size of the reorder buffer, the window of instructions in flight, in cores from 1995 to 2024. <bookmark mark='a'/> Intel's Pentium Pro, the first mass-market out-of-order x86: forty instructions. The MIPS R10000 and the Alpha 21264, the great RISC designs of the late 1990s: thirty-two and eighty. <bookmark mark='b'/> Through the 2000s and 2010s the window grew steadily: about two hundred in Haswell, Skylake and AMD's first Zen. <bookmark mark='c'/> And then it took off. Intel's Sunny Cove, three hundred fifty-two; Golden Cove, in 2021, five hundred twelve; AMD's Zen 5, four hundred forty-eight. Apple's M1 core of 2020 publishes no number, but careful measurement puts its window at about six hundred thirty. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our core's hundred twenty-eight sits in the middle of the history, and we have seen that on the Job even that is rarely full.
735d24470fef.zh: 真实的机器把这一切推到了多远？这是 1995 年到 2024 年间各个处理器核的重排序缓冲区大小，也就是在途指令的窗口。<bookmark mark='a'/>英特尔的 Pentium Pro，第一款面向大众市场的乱序 x86：四十条指令。MIPS R10000 和 Alpha 21264，二十世纪九十年代末伟大的精简指令集设计：三十二和八十。<bookmark mark='b'/>整个二十一世纪头二十年，窗口稳步增长：Haswell、Skylake 和 AMD 的第一代 Zen 大约两百。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后它猛增。英特尔的 Sunny Cove 三百五十二；2021 年的 Golden Cove 五百一十二；AMD 的 Zen 5 四百四十八。苹果 2020 年的 M1 核没有公布数字，但仔细的测量把它的窗口定在大约六百三十。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们的核的一百二十八位于这段历史的中间，而我们已经看到，在任务上即便这么大也很少装满。

fbbb6e6a7fe6.en: Why build windows of hundreds when, as chapter seven showed, a wrong guess drains them? <bookmark mark='a'/> Because of memory. A load that misses every cache waits hundreds of cycles for DRAM, and a core that wants to keep working through such a miss needs hundreds of other instructions to do. Part 9 measures that wait. <bookmark mark='b'/> A big window only pays if the core predicts well enough to fill it, which is why predictors grew alongside: modern TAGE-style predictors miss only a few branches in every thousand instructions on typical code, far fewer than the Job's data-dependent length test. <bookmark mark='c'/> Decode widths grew too: three instructions a cycle in the Pentium Pro, four in Core 2, six in Golden Cove, eight in Apple's M1. <bookmark mark='d'/> The price is area and power. The rename tables, the issue queues and the wakeup logic are among the largest and hottest structures on a modern chip, and they are why Part 10's power wall arrived when it did.
fbbb6e6a7fe6.zh: 既然第七章表明一次猜错就会把窗口清空，为什么还要造几百项的窗口？<bookmark mark='a'/>因为存储器。一次错过所有缓存的取数要等动态随机存储器几百个周期，一个想在这样的缺失期间继续工作的核，需要几百条别的指令可做。第9部分会测量这段等待。<bookmark mark='b'/>大窗口只有在核预测得足够好、能填满它时才划算，所以预测器也随之成长：现代 TAGE 类预测器在典型代码上每一千条指令只猜错几个分支，远少于任务里依赖数据的长度检查。<bookmark mark='c'/>译码宽度也在增长：Pentium Pro 每周期三条，Core 2 四条，Golden Cove 六条，苹果 M1 八条。<bookmark mark='d'/>代价是面积和功耗。重命名表、发射队列和唤醒逻辑是现代芯片上最大、最热的结构之一，也正是它们让第10部分的功耗墙在那个时候到来。

bc3e6fda60a4.en: Nobody has to take these numbers on faith. <bookmark mark='a'/> The vendors publish optimization manuals describing their cores. Agner Fog's guides, updated for decades, describe nearly every x86 core's pipeline. The uops.info project measured the latency, throughput and execution ports of every x86 instruction on every recent core. Independent writers measure the structures vendors do not disclose. <bookmark mark='b'/> And on any Linux machine, perf stat reads the core's own counters: instructions, cycles, branch misses, machine clears. Everything in this part can be seen on the computer in front of you.
bc3e6fda60a4.zh: 没有人需要凭信任接受这些数字。<bookmark mark='a'/>厂商发布描述自己处理器核的优化手册。阿格纳·福格的指南几十年来不断更新，描述了几乎每一款 x86 核的流水线。uops.info 项目测量了每款近期核上每条 x86 指令的延迟、吞吐量和执行端口。独立的作者测量厂商不公开的结构。<bookmark mark='b'/>在任何一台 Linux 机器上，perf stat 都能读出核自己的计数器：指令数、周期数、分支预测失误、机器清除。这一部分的一切，都能在你面前的这台计算机上看到。

b9c57bdf8b6c.en: Chapter fourteen. The Job out of order.
b9c57bdf8b6c.zh: 第十四章。乱序执行的任务。

83ef0d3e2bac.en: Where do the cycles go now? Measure cycles per instruction on the first chapter, and split it. <bookmark mark='a'/> A four-wide core could at best spend a quarter of a cycle on each instruction. <bookmark mark='b'/> With perfect prediction it spends about a third: the rest of that is true dependences, the one-taken-branch fetch limit, and the memory ports. <bookmark mark='c'/> With the real predictor, another fifth of a cycle per instruction goes to wrong guesses. <bookmark mark='d'/> Part 7's pipeline, for comparison, spent one point two. <bookmark mark='e'/> So forty percent of the core's time goes to recovering from mispredictions, nearly all of them in one branch: the scan loop's test of whether an entry has the word's length. That branch depends on the text, and no history predicts it well. The fix is not in the hardware; it is in the program, and Part 17 makes it.
83ef0d3e2bac.zh: 现在周期都去哪儿了？在第一章上测量每条指令的周期数，再把它拆开。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个四槽核最多只能在每条指令上花四分之一个周期。<bookmark mark='b'/>完美预测时它花大约三分之一：多出来的是真依赖、每周期一个跳转的取指限制，以及访存端口。<bookmark mark='c'/>用真实的预测器，每条指令又有五分之一个周期花在猜错上。<bookmark mark='d'/>作为对比，第7部分的流水线花一点二。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以核百分之四十的时间花在从预测错误中恢复，几乎全来自一个分支：扫描循环里检查表项长度是否与单词相同的那个。这个分支取决于文本，没有哪种历史能把它预测好。修复不在硬件里，而在程序里，第17部分会做到。

6917ceba2973.en: Simulating thirty novels on this core, cycle by cycle, would take about a month: it runs about thirty-five thousand instructions a second. So, as in Part 7, we count. <bookmark mark='a'/> Twenty-four passages of four hundred to four thousand bytes, from random books, are run on the core. <bookmark mark='b'/> Their cycle counts are fitted as a linear function of the events in each text that the Job's work depends on: the words, the entries scanned, the entries of the same length, and so on. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then the model is checked on a passage four times longer than any it was fitted on, sixteen thousand bytes of Moby-Dick: six and a half million instructions, three point three million cycles, predicted to within a tenth of a percent.
6917ceba2973.zh: 在这个核上一个周期一个周期地模拟三十部小说，大约要一个月：它每秒只跑大约三万五千条指令。所以，像第7部分那样，我们改为计数。<bookmark mark='a'/>从随机的书里取二十四段四百到四千字节的文字，在核上运行。<bookmark mark='b'/>把它们的周期数拟合成每段文本中那些决定任务工作量的事件的线性函数：单词、扫描过的表项、长度相同的表项，等等。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后在一段比拟合所用的任何一段都长四倍的文字上检验这个模型，《白鲸》的一万六千字节：六百五十万条指令，三百三十万个周期，预测误差在千分之一以内。

95d90738fde5.en: Applied to the whole corpus, the model gives a hundred seven billion instructions in fifty-one billion cycles: two point one instructions per cycle. <bookmark mark='a'/> We keep Part 7's clock of eight hundred eighty-five megahertz. That is generous: renaming, wakeup and the reorder buffer add logic, and a real out-of-order core needs more pipeline stages to hold the same clock. Part 10 returns to clocks. <bookmark mark='b'/> The thirty novels now take fifty-seven seconds, against two minutes twenty-five on the pipeline and four minutes forty on the single-cycle Pebble. <bookmark mark='c'/> That is the third row of the ledger: two and a half times faster again, for exactly the same program. The rows still to come are caches, more cores, a compiler, and then, at last, better algorithms.
95d90738fde5.zh: 用到整个语料上，模型给出一千零七十亿条指令、五百一十亿个周期：每周期二点一条指令。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们沿用第7部分八百八十五兆赫的时钟。这是宽厚的假设：重命名、唤醒和重排序缓冲区都会增加逻辑，一个真实的乱序核需要更多的流水级才能保持同样的时钟。第10部分会回到时钟。<bookmark mark='b'/>三十部小说现在需要五十七秒，而流水线需要两分二十五秒，单周期的 Pebble 需要四分四十秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>这是账本的第三行：又快了两倍半，程序完全相同。接下来的几行是缓存、更多的核、编译器，最后终于是更好的算法。

b6f77108d6e8.en: Chapter fifteen. Frontier: past the dataflow limit, safely.
b6f77108d6e8.zh: 第十五章。前沿：越过数据流极限，而且安全。

a9f5d07c57d4.en: Two questions are open at the edge of this part. The first: can a machine beat the dataflow limit itself? The critical path is a chain of true dependences, and nothing we have built can shorten it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Unless the machine guesses values, not just branches. If a load usually returns the same value as last time, or the last value plus a fixed step, predict it, let the instructions that need it start at once, and check when the real value arrives. Mikko Lipasti and his colleagues proposed this in 1996. <bookmark mark='b'/> We tried it on the Job, in the limit study, with a stride predictor for each load that only guesses after it has been right several times in a row. <bookmark mark='c'/> Without prediction, three point three four instructions per cycle. A predictor that never erred would give three point nine eight. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the real predictor, at every confidence level, makes the machine slower. Its confident guesses are right only sixty to ninety percent of the time, and each wrong one costs a full recovery, which outweighs the dependences broken by the right ones.
a9f5d07c57d4.zh: 在这一部分的边缘，有两个悬而未决的问题。第一个：一台机器能不能打破数据流极限本身？关键路径是一条真依赖链，我们造的任何东西都缩短不了它。<bookmark mark='a'/>除非机器猜的不只是分支，还有值。如果一次取数通常返回和上次相同的值，或者上次的值加一个固定步长，那就预测它，让需要它的指令马上开始，等真值到了再检查。米科·利帕斯蒂和同事在 1996 年提出了这个想法。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们在极限研究里对任务试了一下，给每条取数配一个步长预测器，它只在连续猜对几次之后才开始猜。<bookmark mark='c'/>不做预测时，每周期三点三四条指令。一个从不出错的预测器会给出三点九八。<bookmark mark='d'/>而真实的预测器在每一个置信水平上都让机器变慢。它有把握的猜测只有百分之六十到九十是对的，每次猜错都要一次完整的恢复，代价超过了猜对时打破的依赖。

e634552adf2a.en: That matches what researchers found. <bookmark mark='a'/> A value predictor must be right far more than ninety-nine percent of the time to pay its way. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2014 Arthur Perais and André Seznec showed a design that does it, using very high confidence thresholds and repairing mistakes cheaply at commit, and revived a field many had given up. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the Job, though, even perfect value prediction would buy only nineteen percent, because the branches, not the loads, set the limit. <bookmark mark='d'/> Which programs have values worth guessing, and whether a core can find them cheaply, is still an open question.
e634552adf2a.zh: 这和研究者的发现相符。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个数值预测器的正确率必须远高于百分之九十九才划得来。<bookmark mark='b'/>2014 年，阿瑟·佩雷和安德烈·塞兹内克展示了一个做到这一点的设计，用非常高的置信阈值，并在提交时廉价地修复错误，复兴了一个许多人已经放弃的领域。<bookmark mark='c'/>不过在任务上，即使完美的数值预测也只能换来百分之十九，因为设定极限的是分支，而不是取数。<bookmark mark='d'/>哪些程序有值得猜的值，核能不能廉价地找到它们，仍然是一个开放的问题。

8c78503f1f4b.en: The second question: can speculation be made safe, without giving up its speed? Spectre works because a speculatively loaded value is passed on to a second load whose address it chooses, and that second load leaves a footprint in the cache. <bookmark mark='a'/> So here is a rule for our core, in the spirit of two 2019 proposals, Speculative Taint Tracking and NDA. A load that completes while some older branch is still unresolved keeps its value to itself: nothing that depends on it may run until every older branch has executed. <bookmark mark='b'/> Run the attack against this core: the probe shows no fast line, and nothing leaks. <bookmark mark='c'/> Run the Job: three and a half percent slower. <bookmark mark='d'/> Cheap, here, because the speculation that remains is the useful kind: arithmetic, branches, and loads whose addresses are already known can all still run ahead.
