8c78503f1f4b.zh: 第二个问题：推测执行能不能在不放弃速度的前提下变得安全？幽灵之所以奏效，是因为一个推测读出的值被传给了第二次取数，由它选择第二次取数的地址，而第二次取数在缓存里留下了足迹。<bookmark mark='a'/>所以这里给我们的核定一条规则，借鉴 2019 年的两个提案：推测污点追踪和 NDA。一次在某个更老的分支尚未解决时完成的取数，把它的值留给自己：依赖它的任何东西都不能执行，直到每个更老的分支都执行完。<bookmark mark='b'/>用这个核去跑攻击：探测显示没有快的那一行，什么也没泄露。<bookmark mark='c'/>跑任务：慢百分之三点五。<bookmark mark='d'/>在这里之所以便宜，是因为剩下的推测都是有用的那种：算术、分支，以及地址已经知道的取数，都还可以往前跑。

92b6f9da63c8.en: Here is where the research stands. <bookmark mark='a'/> Does a rule like ours block every leak of speculatively loaded data, or only the one we tried? Since 2020, researchers have defined what it means for a program to be safe under speculation, speculative non-interference, and built tools that check it; proving a whole core safe is still out of reach. <bookmark mark='b'/> What does safety cost? Published hardware schemes report from a few percent to tens of percent, depending on how much they protect. Nobody knows the floor. <bookmark mark='c'/> The cache is not the only channel: execution ports, the predictors themselves, and power draw have all been used to leak. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the oldest question of all: the Job contains two thousand four hundred instructions per cycle of parallelism, and we use two. Runahead execution, windows of thousands of instructions, and dataflow machines have all tried to reach it. The problem with a star at the end of this part starts here.
92b6f9da63c8.zh: 研究的现状是这样的。<bookmark mark='a'/>像我们这样的规则，能挡住每一种推测读出数据的泄露，还是只挡住了我们试过的这一种？自 2020 年起，研究者定义了一个程序在推测下安全意味着什么，即推测非干涉，并造出了检查它的工具；证明一整个核是安全的，仍然遥不可及。<bookmark mark='b'/>安全要付出多少代价？已发表的硬件方案报告的代价从百分之几到百分之几十，取决于它们保护多少。没有人知道下限在哪里。<bookmark mark='c'/>缓存不是唯一的信道：执行端口、预测器本身，乃至功耗，都曾被用来泄露信息。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有最老的问题：任务里有每周期两千四百条指令的并行性，我们只用了两条。超前执行、几千条指令的窗口和数据流机器都曾试图够到它。这一部分最后那道带星号的题，就从这里开始。

8a90cc3b1ee3.en: What we built in this part. The dataflow graph, and the limit its critical path sets on any machine. Register renaming, which removes every false dependence. The scoreboard and Tomasulo's algorithm, cycle by cycle. A real out-of-order core with a reorder buffer, checked against the emulator, whose exceptions stay precise. The wall it hits: parallelism by the thousand, hidden behind branches nobody can predict. Spectre, run on our own machine, and two fixes measured. And the next row of the ledger: the same Job, two and a half times faster again.
8a90cc3b1ee3.zh: 我们在这一部分造了什么。数据流图，以及它的关键路径给任何机器设下的极限。寄存器重命名，它消除了每一个假依赖。记分牌和托马苏洛算法，一个周期一个周期地看。一个带重排序缓冲区的真实乱序核，与仿真器核对过，它的异常保持精确。它撞上的墙：成千上万的并行性，藏在没人能预测的分支后面。在我们自己的机器上跑的幽灵攻击，以及测量过的两种修复。还有账本的下一行：同一个任务，又快了两倍半。

fccebeeebeff.en: Where this comes back. The big windows exist to hide memory's latency, which Part 9 measures and caches attack. The ILP wall, and the power that width costs, lead to Part 10's multicore and vector machines. Static scheduling and software pipelining are Part 13's compiler at work. The branch no predictor can learn is removed by changing the algorithm, in Parts 16 and 17. A core that reorders loads and stores raises the question of what other threads can see, which is Part 33's memory models. Spectre and Meltdown return with the kernel, virtual memory, and Part 55. And VLIW's second life is in the domain-specific hardware of Part 60.
fccebeeebeff.zh: 这些会在哪里再出现。大窗口是为了藏起存储器的延迟，第9部分测量它，缓存对付它。指令级并行之墙，以及宽度要付出的功耗，通向第10部分的多核和向量机器。静态调度和软件流水是第13部分编译器的工作。没有预测器能学会的那个分支，要靠改变算法来去掉，在第16和第17部分。一个重排取数和存数的核引出了其他线程能看到什么的问题，那是第33部分的存储器模型。幽灵和熔断会随着内核、虚拟存储器以及第55部分回来。而超长指令字的第二次生命，在第60部分的领域专用硬件里。

e024d6904e3b.en: In practice. CPU design teams at Apple, Arm, AMD, Intel and Qualcomm tune predictors, schedulers and windows on simulators like ours, at a vastly larger scale. Performance engineers read IPC, branch misses and machine clears from the counters, and use top-down analysis to see where issue slots go. Spectre mitigations live in every kernel, in browsers' site isolation, and in clouds' policies on sharing cores. Open out-of-order RISC-V cores, like Berkeley's BOOM and China's XiangShan, can be read line by line. And research uses simulators such as gem5 and ChampSim.
e024d6904e3b.zh: 实践中。苹果、Arm、AMD、英特尔和高通的处理器设计团队，在像我们这样的模拟器上调整预测器、调度器和窗口，只是规模大得多。性能工程师从计数器里读出每周期指令数、分支预测失误和机器清除，用自顶向下的分析看发射槽都去了哪里。幽灵的缓解措施存在于每个内核里、浏览器的站点隔离里，以及云平台关于共享处理器核的策略里。开源的乱序 RISC-V 核，比如伯克利的 BOOM 和中国的香山，可以一行一行地读。研究则使用 gem5 和 ChampSim 这样的模拟器。

2e9f188b732f.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: take Part 7's hand-scheduling fix to the out-of-order core, and see what it is worth there. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: nobody knows its full answer, and the notes say where to start.
2e9f188b732f.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在这一部分的笔记里。可以在任何一道上暂停。第五道是动手题：把第7部分手工调度的那个修复搬到乱序核上，看看它在那里值多少。最后一道标了星号，是研究题：没有人知道它的完整答案，笔记里说明了从哪里入手。

3a3bd0c7de5b.en: Next time. Two of Pebble's five stages were a whole nanosecond of memory, and a real DRAM access takes hundreds of cycles. Part 9 builds the memory hierarchy: caches, locality, the miss rate curves of the Job, a latency staircase measured on this very computer, and a theorem about pebbles that says how much data any matrix multiply must move.
3a3bd0c7de5b.zh: 下一次。Pebble 的五个流水级里有两个是整整一纳秒的存储器访问，而一次真实的动态随机存储器访问要几百个周期。第9部分建造存储层次：缓存、局部性、任务的缺失率曲线、在这台计算机上实测的延迟阶梯，以及一个关于卵石的定理，它说明任何矩阵乘法必须搬动多少数据。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分依据的书和论文都在屏幕上，也在笔记里。感谢观看。
